+package resource
+
+// Coverage for the run-level enable_caching override (RuntimeConfig.EnableCaching)
+// on direct runs and on every recurring-run execution path.
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/backend/src/apiserver/common"
+	"github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/backend/src/apiserver/model"
+	"github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/backend/src/apiserver/template"
+	"github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/backend/src/common/util"
+	"github.com/spf13/viper"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+	v1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
+)
+
+// nestedCachingPipeline has tasks under ExitHandler, dsl.If, ParallelFor and
+// a sub-pipeline, so only a traversal of nested DAGs reaches all of them.
+const nestedCachingPipelineTasks = 9
+
+func nestedCachingPipeline(t *testing.T) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	raw, err := os.ReadFile("../template/testdata/caching_override/input.yaml")
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return string(raw)
+}
+
+// taskCaching returns the enable_cache setting of every task in every DAG.
+func taskCaching(t *testing.T, manifest model.LargeText) map[string]bool {
+	t.Helper()
+	tmpl, err := template.New([]byte(manifest), template.TemplateOptions{})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	spec := tmpl.(*template.V2Spec).PipelineSpec()
+	got := map[string]bool{}
+	for name, task := range spec.GetRoot().GetDag().GetTasks() {
+		got["root/"+name] = task.GetCachingOptions().GetEnableCache()
+	}
+	for component, spec := range spec.GetComponents() {
+		for name, task := range spec.GetDag().GetTasks() {
+			got[component+"/"+name] = task.GetCachingOptions().GetEnableCache()
+		}
+	}
+	return got
+}
+
+func requireAllTasksCaching(t *testing.T, manifest model.LargeText, want bool) {
+	t.Helper()
+	got := taskCaching(t, manifest)
+	require.Len(t, got, nestedCachingPipelineTasks)
+	for task, enabled := range got {
+		require.Equal(t, want, enabled, "enable_cache of task %s", task)
+	}
+}
+
+func setMultiUserMode(t *testing.T, enabled bool) {
+	t.Helper()
+	previous := viper.Get(common.MultiUserMode)
+	viper.Set(common.MultiUserMode, enabled)
+	t.Cleanup(func() { viper.Set(common.MultiUserMode, previous) })
+}
+
+func initWithNestedCachingVersion(t *testing.T) (*FakeClientManager, *ResourceManager, *model.Experiment, *model.PipelineVersion) {
+	t.Helper()
+	store, manager, experiment := initWithExperiment(t)
+	pipeline, err := manager.CreatePipeline(createPipeline("nested-caching", "", "ns1"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	version, err := manager.CreatePipelineVersion(createPipelineVersion(pipeline.UUID, "v1", "", "", nestedCachingPipeline(t), "", "ns1"))
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return store, manager, experiment, version
+}
+
+var enableCachingCases = []struct {
+	name          string
+	enableCaching *bool
+}{
+	{"unset", nil},
+	{"false", util.BoolPointer(false)},
+	{"true", util.BoolPointer(true)},
+}
+
+// The driver reads task specs from the manifest stored with the run, so the
+// override must be in that manifest. The uploaded version must not change.
+func TestCreateRun_EnableCaching(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, source := range []string{"version reference", "inline spec"} {
+		for _, tc := range enableCachingCases {
+			t.Run(source+"/"+tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+				store, manager, experiment, version := initWithNestedCachingVersion(t)
+				defer store.Close()
+				pipelineSpec := model.PipelineSpec{RuntimeConfig: model.RuntimeConfig{EnableCaching: tc.enableCaching}}
+				if source == "inline spec" {
+					pipelineSpec.PipelineSpecManifest = model.LargeText(nestedCachingPipeline(t))
+				} else {
+					pipelineSpec.PipelineId = version.PipelineId
+					pipelineSpec.PipelineVersionId = version.UUID
+				}
+				created, err := manager.CreateRun(context.Background(), &model.Run{
+					DisplayName: "run", Namespace: "ns1", ExperimentId: experiment.UUID, PipelineSpec: pipelineSpec,
+				})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+
+				stored, err := manager.GetRun(created.UUID)
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, tc.enableCaching, stored.EnableCaching)
+				if tc.enableCaching == nil {
+					require.Equal(t, taskCaching(t, model.LargeText(nestedCachingPipeline(t))), taskCaching(t, stored.PipelineSpecManifest))
+				} else {
+					requireAllTasksCaching(t, stored.PipelineSpecManifest, *tc.enableCaching)
+				}
+				unchanged, err := manager.GetPipelineVersion(version.UUID)
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, version.PipelineSpec, unchanged.PipelineSpec, "the uploaded pipeline version must not change")
+			})
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// The override only changes task settings; the deployment-wide setting is
+// passed to the driver separately and still disables caching.
+func TestCreateRun_EnableCachingKeepsDeploymentDisable(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, cacheDisabled := range []bool{false, true} {
+		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("CacheDisabled=%t", cacheDisabled), func(t *testing.T) {
+			store, manager, experiment, version := initWithNestedCachingVersion(t)
+			defer store.Close()
+			manager.options.CacheDisabled = cacheDisabled
+			created, err := manager.CreateRun(context.Background(), &model.Run{
+				DisplayName: "run", Namespace: "ns1", ExperimentId: experiment.UUID,
+				PipelineSpec: model.PipelineSpec{
+					PipelineVersionId: version.UUID,
+					RuntimeConfig:     model.RuntimeConfig{EnableCaching: util.BoolPointer(true)},
+				},
+			})
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			requireAllTasksCaching(t, created.PipelineSpecManifest, true)
+			workflow := string(created.PipelineRuntimeManifest)
+			require.Contains(t, workflow, fmt.Sprintf(`"cache_disabled":%t`, cacheDisabled))
+			require.NotContains(t, workflow, fmt.Sprintf(`"cache_disabled":%t`, !cacheDisabled))
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// Single-user schedules pinned to a version or an inline spec embed a
+// compiled workflow that the controller submits without calling CreateRun.
+// The persistence agent's report then creates the run from the job, so the
+// job must store the effective manifest, and reconciliation after a restart
+// must keep it.
+func TestCreateJob_EnableCachingPinnedSingleUser(t *testing.T) {
+	setMultiUserMode(t, false)
+	for _, source := range []string{"version reference", "inline spec"} {
+		for _, tc := range enableCachingCases {
+			t.Run(source+"/"+tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+				store, manager, experiment, version := initWithNestedCachingVersion(t)
+				defer store.Close()
+				pipelineSpec := model.PipelineSpec{RuntimeConfig: model.RuntimeConfig{EnableCaching: tc.enableCaching}}
+				if source == "inline spec" {
+					pipelineSpec.PipelineSpecManifest = model.LargeText(nestedCachingPipeline(t))
+				} else {
+					pipelineSpec.PipelineVersionId = version.UUID
+				}
+				job, err := manager.CreateJob(context.Background(), &model.Job{
+					DisplayName: "pinned", Namespace: "ns1", ExperimentId: experiment.UUID, Enabled: true, MaxConcurrency: 1,
+					PipelineSpec: pipelineSpec,
+				})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				swfClient := store.SwfClient().ScheduledWorkflow(job.Namespace)
+				swf, err := swfClient.Get(context.Background(), job.K8SName, v1.GetOptions{})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.NotNil(t, swf.Spec.Workflow.Spec, "the controller submits the embedded workflow")
+
+				// A new manager reads the job back from the database, as after a restart.
+				restarted := NewResourceManager(store, &ResourceManagerOptions{CollectMetrics: false})
+				stored, err := restarted.GetJob(job.UUID)
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, tc.enableCaching, stored.EnableCaching)
+				require.NoError(t, restarted.ReconcileSwfCrs(context.Background()))
+				reconciled, err := swfClient.Get(context.Background(), job.K8SName, v1.GetOptions{})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, swf.Spec, reconciled.Spec, "reconciliation must keep the override")
+
+				reported, err := restarted.recurringRunReportPipelineSpec(stored, testWorkflowWithoutStatus(), "run-id")
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, tc.enableCaching, reported.EnableCaching)
+				if tc.enableCaching == nil {
+					require.Equal(t, taskCaching(t, model.LargeText(nestedCachingPipeline(t))), taskCaching(t, reported.PipelineSpecManifest))
+				} else {
+					requireAllTasksCaching(t, reported.PipelineSpecManifest, *tc.enableCaching)
+				}
+			})
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// Single-user schedules that follow the latest version run through CreateRun.
+// The ScheduledWorkflow carries the override for the controller to send, and
+// it is applied after the run's version is resolved. A request without the
+// field (a ScheduledWorkflow without a workflow resource) uses the job's value.
+func TestCreateJob_EnableCachingFollowLatestSingleUser(t *testing.T) {
+	setMultiUserMode(t, false)
+	for _, sendOverride := range []bool{true, false} {
+		for _, tc := range enableCachingCases[1:] {
+			t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("%s/sent=%t", tc.name, sendOverride), func(t *testing.T) {
+				store, manager, experiment, version := initWithNestedCachingVersion(t)
+				defer store.Close()
+				job, err := manager.CreateJob(context.Background(), &model.Job{
+					DisplayName: "latest", Namespace: "ns1", ExperimentId: experiment.UUID, Enabled: true, MaxConcurrency: 1,
+					PipelineSpec: model.PipelineSpec{
+						PipelineId:    version.PipelineId,
+						RuntimeConfig: model.RuntimeConfig{EnableCaching: tc.enableCaching},
+					},
+				})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Empty(t, job.PipelineVersionId)
+				swf, err := store.SwfClient().ScheduledWorkflow(job.Namespace).Get(context.Background(), job.K8SName, v1.GetOptions{})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Nil(t, swf.Spec.Workflow.Spec)
+				require.Equal(t, tc.enableCaching, swf.Spec.Workflow.EnableCaching)
+
+				// The request the controller builds from the ScheduledWorkflow.
+				runtimeConfig := model.RuntimeConfig{}
+				if sendOverride {
+					runtimeConfig.EnableCaching = swf.Spec.Workflow.EnableCaching
+				}
+				created, err := manager.CreateRun(context.Background(), &model.Run{
+					DisplayName: "tick", Namespace: job.Namespace, ExperimentId: job.ExperimentId, RecurringRunId: job.UUID,
+					PipelineSpec: model.PipelineSpec{PipelineId: swf.Spec.PipelineId, RuntimeConfig: runtimeConfig},
+				})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, version.UUID, created.PipelineVersionId)
+				require.Equal(t, tc.enableCaching, created.EnableCaching)
+				requireAllTasksCaching(t, created.PipelineSpecManifest, *tc.enableCaching)
+
+				// A report that wins the race restores the same effective manifest.
+				workflow := testWorkflowWithoutStatus()
+				workflow.SetAnnotations(recurringRunPipelineVersionAnnotation, version.UUID)
+				reported, err := manager.recurringRunReportPipelineSpec(job, workflow, "run-id")
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, created.PipelineSpecManifest, reported.PipelineSpecManifest)
+			})
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// In multi-user mode the controller sends only the recurring run ID, and the
+// API server restores execution inputs from the stored job.
+func TestCreateJob_EnableCachingMultiUser(t *testing.T) {
+	setMultiUserMode(t, true)
+	for _, pinned := range []bool{true, false} {
+		for _, tc := range enableCachingCases {
+			t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("pinned=%t/%s", pinned, tc.name), func(t *testing.T) {
+				store, manager, experiment, version := initWithNestedCachingVersion(t)
+				defer store.Close()
+				manager.time = fixedRecurringTime{epoch: 200}
+				ctx := multiUserContext()
+				pipelineSpec := model.PipelineSpec{PipelineId: version.PipelineId, RuntimeConfig: model.RuntimeConfig{EnableCaching: tc.enableCaching}}
+				if pinned {
+					pipelineSpec.PipelineVersionId = version.UUID
+				}
+				job, err := manager.CreateJob(ctx, &model.Job{
+					DisplayName: "schedule", Namespace: "ns1", ExperimentId: experiment.UUID, Enabled: true, MaxConcurrency: 1,
+					Trigger: model.Trigger{PeriodicSchedule: model.PeriodicSchedule{
+						PeriodicScheduleStartTimeInSec: util.Int64Pointer(100), IntervalSecond: util.Int64Pointer(10),
+					}},
+					PipelineSpec: pipelineSpec,
+				})
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+
+				// The controller's request, restored by a manager that reads the job back from the database.
+				restarted := NewResourceManager(store, &ResourceManagerOptions{CollectMetrics: false})
+				restarted.time = fixedRecurringTime{epoch: 200}
+				run := &model.Run{DisplayName: "tick", RecurringRunId: job.UUID}
+				require.NoError(t, restarted.PrepareRecurringRun(ctx, run))
+				require.Equal(t, tc.enableCaching, run.EnableCaching)
+				created, err := restarted.CreateRun(ctx, run)
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, version.UUID, created.PipelineVersionId)
+				stored, err := restarted.GetRun(created.UUID)
+				require.NoError(t, err)
+				require.Equal(t, tc.enableCaching, stored.EnableCaching)
+				if tc.enableCaching == nil {
+					require.Equal(t, taskCaching(t, version.PipelineSpec), taskCaching(t, stored.PipelineSpecManifest))
+				} else {
+					requireAllTasksCaching(t, stored.PipelineSpecManifest, *tc.enableCaching)
+				}
+			})
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func TestCreateRun_EnableCachingRejectedWithoutPipelineSpec(t *testing.T) {
+	store, manager, experiment := initWithExperiment(t)
+	defer store.Close()
+	_, err := manager.CreateRun(context.Background(), &model.Run{
+		DisplayName: "run", Namespace: "ns1", ExperimentId: experiment.UUID,
+		PipelineSpec: model.PipelineSpec{
+			PipelineSpecManifest: "kind: ConfigMap\n",
+			RuntimeConfig:        model.RuntimeConfig{EnableCaching: util.BoolPointer(false)},
+		},
+	})
+	require.Error(t, err)
+	require.True(t, strings.Contains(err.Error(), "pipeline spec"), err.Error())

+func TestEnableCachingRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, enableCaching := range []*bool{nil, proto.Bool(false), proto.Bool(true)} {
+		name := "unset"

+			name = fmt.Sprint(*enableCaching)
+		}
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var runtimeConfig *apiv2.RuntimeConfig
+			if enableCaching != nil {
+				runtimeConfig = &apiv2.RuntimeConfig{EnableCaching: proto.Bool(*enableCaching)}
+			}
+
+			modelRun, err := toModelRun(&apiv2.Run{
+				DisplayName:   "run",
+				RuntimeConfig: runtimeConfig,
+				PipelineSource: &apiv2.Run_PipelineVersionReference{
+					PipelineVersionReference: &apiv2.PipelineVersionReference{PipelineId: "p1", PipelineVersionId: "v1"},
+				},
+			})
+			require.NoError(t, err)
+			assert.Equal(t, enableCaching, modelRun.EnableCaching)
+			assert.True(t, proto.Equal(runtimeConfig, toAPIRun(modelRun).GetRuntimeConfig()), "run: %v", toAPIRun(modelRun).GetRuntimeConfig())
+
+			modelJob, err := toModelJob(&apiv2.RecurringRun{
+				DisplayName:    "job",

+				RuntimeConfig:  runtimeConfig,
+				Trigger: &apiv2.Trigger{Trigger: &apiv2.Trigger_PeriodicSchedule{

+				PipelineSource: &apiv2.RecurringRun_PipelineVersionReference{

+				},
+			})

+			assert.Equal(t, enableCaching, modelJob.EnableCaching)
+			assert.True(t, proto.Equal(runtimeConfig, toAPIRecurringRun(modelJob).GetRuntimeConfig()), "recurring run: %v", toAPIRecurringRun(modelJob).GetRuntimeConfig())

+package template
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+
+	"github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/api/v2alpha1/go/pipelinespec"
+	"github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/backend/src/common/util"
+	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"
+)
+
+// withCachingOverride returns a copy of spec in which every task of every DAG
+// reachable from the root has caching set to enableCaching. It matches the
+// SDK's _override_caching_options, so a run behaves the same whether the
+// client rewrites an inline spec or the server rewrites a referenced version.
+// Cache keys are left unchanged.
+func withCachingOverride(spec *pipelinespec.PipelineSpec, enableCaching bool) *pipelinespec.PipelineSpec {
+	out := proto.Clone(spec).(*pipelinespec.PipelineSpec)
+	// Tasks inside dsl.If, ParallelFor, ExitHandler and nested pipelines live
+	// in the DAGs of their parent components, not in the root DAG.
+	dags := []*pipelinespec.DagSpec{out.GetRoot().GetDag()}
+	visited := map[string]bool{}
+	for len(dags) > 0 {
+		dag := dags[len(dags)-1]
+		dags = dags[:len(dags)-1]
+		for _, task := range dag.GetTasks() {
+			if task.CachingOptions == nil {
+				task.CachingOptions = &pipelinespec.PipelineTaskSpec_CachingOptions{}
+			}
+			task.CachingOptions.EnableCache = enableCaching
+			name := task.GetComponentRef().GetName()
+			if visited[name] {
+				continue
+			}
+			if component, ok := out.GetComponents()[name]; ok && component.GetDag() != nil {
+				visited[name] = true
+				dags = append(dags, component.GetDag())
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return out
+}
+
+// ApplyCachingOverride returns manifest with a run's enable_caching override
+// applied to its pipeline spec. A nil override returns manifest unchanged.
+//
+// Drivers read task specs from the manifest stored with the run, so the
+// override must be applied to that manifest, not only to the compiled
+// workflow. The result is encoded the same way as stored pipeline versions,
+// and any platform spec is kept.
+func ApplyCachingOverride(manifest []byte, enableCaching *bool) ([]byte, error) {
+	if enableCaching == nil {
+		return manifest, nil
+	}
+	tmpl, err := NewV2SpecTemplate(manifest, TemplateOptions{})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, util.Wrap(err, "Failed to apply enable_caching to the pipeline spec")
+	}
+	tmpl.spec = withCachingOverride(tmpl.spec, *enableCaching)
+	bytes := tmpl.Bytes()
+	if bytes == nil {
+		return nil, util.NewInternalServerError(errors.New("cannot encode the pipeline spec"), "Failed to apply enable_caching to the pipeline spec")
+	}
+	return bytes, nil
+}

+)
+
+const cachingOverrideTestdata = "testdata/caching_override/"
+
+func readTestFile(t *testing.T, path string) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	raw, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return raw
+}
+
+// parseSpec parses a manifest the way the server parses uploads (yaml.v3). A
+// YAML 1.1 parser would read the input parameter named "n" as false.
+func parseSpec(t *testing.T, manifest []byte) *V2Spec {
+	t.Helper()
+	tmpl, err := NewV2SpecTemplate(manifest, TemplateOptions{})
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	return tmpl
+}
+
+func loadSpecJSON(t *testing.T, path string) *pipelinespec.PipelineSpec {
+	t.Helper()
+	spec := &pipelinespec.PipelineSpec{}
+	require.NoError(t, protojson.Unmarshal(readTestFile(t, path), spec))
+	return spec
+}
+
+// The JSON fixtures were produced by the SDK's _override_caching_options on
+// input.yaml, so these tests pin server/SDK parity, including tasks nested
+// under ExitHandler, dsl.If, ParallelFor and sub-pipelines.
+func TestWithCachingOverride_MatchesSDK(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		enableCaching bool
+		want          string
+	}{
+		{false, "disabled.json"},
+		{true, "enabled.json"},
+	} {
+		input := parseSpec(t, readTestFile(t, cachingOverrideTestdata+"input.yaml")).spec
+		original := proto.Clone(input)
+		got := withCachingOverride(input, tc.enableCaching)
+		require.Empty(t, cmp.Diff(loadSpecJSON(t, cachingOverrideTestdata+tc.want), got, protocmp.Transform()), tc.want)
+		require.True(t, proto.Equal(original, input), "the input spec must not be modified")
+	}
+}
+
+// The rewritten manifest is what the driver reads, so it must parse back to
+// the SDK result.
+func TestApplyCachingOverride_MatchesSDK(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		enableCaching bool
+		want          string
+	}{
+		{false, "disabled.json"},
+		{true, "enabled.json"},
+	} {
+		got, err := ApplyCachingOverride(readTestFile(t, cachingOverrideTestdata+"input.yaml"), &tc.enableCaching)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		require.Empty(t, cmp.Diff(loadSpecJSON(t, cachingOverrideTestdata+tc.want), parseSpec(t, got).spec, protocmp.Transform()), tc.want)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestApplyCachingOverride_NilKeepsManifest(t *testing.T) {
+	raw := readTestFile(t, cachingOverrideTestdata+"input.yaml")
+	got, err := ApplyCachingOverride(raw, nil)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.Equal(t, raw, got)
+}
+
+func TestApplyCachingOverride_RejectsManifestWithoutPipelineSpec(t *testing.T) {
+	disabled := false
+	_, err := ApplyCachingOverride([]byte("kind: ConfigMap\n"), &disabled)
+	require.Error(t, err)
+}
+
+// The platform spec (volumes, node selectors, ...) is a second YAML document.
+// It must survive the rewrite, executors must not change, and the result
+// must still compile.
+func TestApplyCachingOverride_KeepsPlatformSpecAndExecutors(t *testing.T) {
+	proxy.InitializeConfigWithEmptyForTests()
+	for _, path := range []string{cachingOverrideTestdata + "input.yaml", "testdata/pipeline_with_volume.yaml"} {
+		raw := readTestFile(t, path)
+		before := parseSpec(t, raw)
+		disabled := false
+		got, err := ApplyCachingOverride(raw, &disabled)
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		after := parseSpec(t, got)
+		require.Empty(t, cmp.Diff(before.platformSpec, after.platformSpec, protocmp.Transform()), path)
+		require.Empty(t, cmp.Diff(before.spec.GetDeploymentSpec(), after.spec.GetDeploymentSpec(), protocmp.Transform()), path)
+		for _, task := range after.spec.GetRoot().GetDag().GetTasks() {
+			require.False(t, task.GetCachingOptions().GetEnableCache(), path)
+		}
+		_, err = after.RunWorkflow(&model.Run{DisplayName: "run"}, RunWorkflowOptions{})
+		require.NoError(t, err, path)
+	}
+}

problem_statement.title: feat(backend): honor run-level enable_caching for runs and recurring runs submitted by pipeline reference
problem_statement.body:
### Feature Area

/area backend
/area sdk

### What feature would you like to see?

A run-level `enable_caching` override that works for runs **and recurring runs created from an uploaded pipeline** (`pipeline_version_reference`), applied by the API server. This is the run/recurring-run slice of #10839, scoped as suggested in https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/issues/10839#issuecomment-6802280603.

Today the SDK applies `enable_caching` only by rewriting an inline pipeline spec, so it works for package/function submissions only. For submissions by `pipeline_id`/`version_id`, both `run_pipeline` and `create_recurring_run` silently drop it. A client-side fix cannot keep the version link, because the API accepts an inline spec **or** a version reference, not both (`HTTP 400: oneof ... pipeline_source is already set`).

Reproduced on KFP 2.18.0: `run_pipeline(pipeline_id=..., version_id=..., enable_caching=False)` still produced a cache hit.

### Proposed design

- **API:** add `optional bool enable_caching` to `RuntimeConfig` (`backend/api/v2/runtime_config.proto`), with three states:
  - unset: inherit the compiled task settings (current behavior)
  - `false`: disable caching for every task
  - `true`: enable caching for every task, still subject to deployment-wide `CacheEnabled=false`
- **Server, runs:** after resolving the pipeline version, apply the override to the run's own copy of the pipeline spec, covering all reachable nested DAGs (same traversal as the SDK after #15429). Persist that effective spec, which is what the driver reads via `GetRun`. The uploaded pipeline version stays unchanged.
- **Server, recurring runs:** persist the override with the recurring run and apply it to every execution path. That covers schedules pinned to a version, including single-user schedules where the ScheduledWorkflow controller creates precompiled workflows directly ([controller.go](https://github.com/kubeflow/pipelines/blob/a5e2472ac5799157b0a31bf6f1f9d8b79caf61af/backend/src/crd/controller/scheduledworkflow/controller.go#L637-L687)), and schedules that follow the latest version.
- **SDK:** send `runtime_config.enable_caching` for reference-based submissions. Older servers reject the unknown field with HTTP 400, so surface a clear error in that case rather than silently ignoring it.

### Out of scope (stays in #10839 / #14253)

- `cache_key` for reference-based submissions. It needs its own decision; I won't extend custom cache keys through nested DAGs, since #15429 deliberately kept that separate because loop iterations could share fingerprints. #14253 stays open for that part.
- UI controls and a persistent per-pipeline caching policy.

### Acceptance criteria / tests

- absent / `false` / `true` for inline and reference submissions, for direct runs and recurring runs (version-pinned and latest-version)
- nested DAG tasks (ExitHandler, condition, ParallelFor, sub-pipelines) match the SDK's package-submission result
- the stored run spec round-trips and the uploaded pipeline version is unchanged
- deployment-wide `CacheEnabled=false` still wins over `enable_caching=true`
- SDK request construction, plus the old-server 400 path

### Delivery

I have a working prototype of the spec rewrite with SDK-parity fixtures. Planned PRs:

1. API field, generated clients and storage
2. Server application for runs
3. Recurring-run paths
4. SDK wiring and docs

If you'd prefer one sub-issue per PR so that each PR can use `Fixes #N`, I'm happy to split this.

---

Love this idea? Give it a 👍.

problem_statement.title: INPUTS reuses stale results for zero-column DataFrames with different row indexes
problem_statement.body:
### Bug summary

`INPUTS` gives the same cache key to DataFrames with no columns even when their row indexes differ. A task returning the row count consequently returns the first result without executing for the changed input.

I reproduced this against the current checkout with the local test harness and separate temporary result storage:

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from prefect import task
from prefect.cache_policies import INPUTS
from prefect.testing.utilities import prefect_test_harness

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp, prefect_test_harness():
    @task(cache_policy=INPUTS, persist_result=True, result_storage=Path(temp))
    def row_count(frame):
        return len(frame)

    first = pd.DataFrame(index=[1, 2])
    second = pd.DataFrame(index=[3, 4, 5])
    states = [row_count(frame, return_state=True)
              for frame in (first, second, second.copy())]
    print([state.result() for state in states])
    print([state.name for state in states])
```

Actual: `[2, 2, 2]`, `['Completed', 'Cached', 'Cached']`.
Expected: `[2, 3, 3]`, `['Completed', 'Completed', 'Cached']`.

The async task path gives the same wrong results. Adding a real column makes the control pass. Same-length frames with different Index or MultiIndex labels also collide; a task returning the index labels returns the old labels.

### Version info

```text
Version:              3.9.2+5.g941c57c
API version:          0.8.4
Python version:       3.13.14
Git commit:           941c57c5
Built:                Mon, Nov 09, 2026 11:08 PM
OS/Arch:              darwin/arm64
Profile:              ephemeral
Server type:          ephemeral
Pydantic version:     2.14.1
Server:
  Database:           sqlite
  SQLite version:     3.53.1
```

pandas 2.3.3. All data was synthetic and the API/database/result storage were local; analytics and background services were disabled in the diagnostic harness. No exception is raised by Prefect—the failing check is the returned result.

### Additional context

The registered DataFrame transform in `cache_policies.py` reduces every zero-column frame to `([], [])`. There is no Series left to carry the row index. This is separate from generic hashing collisions: the inputs are already identical before hashing.

I'd like to fix this at that normalizer by including the original Index only when there are no columns, with row-count/Index/MultiIndex and repeat/copy/process-stability regressions. The existing payload and cache keys for frames with columns would stay unchanged. New zero-column keys should not reuse the old collided entries. Does that scope fit the existing cache compatibility expectations?

Found and reproduced with Codex assistance. No implementation PR is open.

problem_statement.title: bug(sdk): kubernetes set_image_pull_secrets, add_init_container and add_ephemeral_volume split plain-string list arguments into single characters
problem_statement.body:
### Environment
- KFP SDK: master @ 28e90e6a6 (install from source)
- Python 3.11, no cluster needed (compile only)

### Steps to reproduce

from kfp import compiler, dsl
from kfp import kubernetes as k8s

@dsl.component
def comp():
    pass

@dsl.pipeline
def pipe():
    t = comp()
    k8s.set_image_pull_secrets(t, secret_names='my-secret')
    # also:
    # k8s.add_init_container(t, name='init', image='busybox', command='echo hi', args='foo')
    # k8s.add_ephemeral_volume(t, volume_name='v', mount_path='/m',
    #                          access_modes='ReadWriteOnce', size='5Gi')

compiler.Compiler().compile(pipe, '/tmp/out.yaml')

### Actual result
No error or warning. The compiled platform spec contains one entry per character:
- set_image_pull_secrets: nine imagePullSecret entries (m, y, -, s, e, c, r, e, t)
- add_init_container: command: [e, c, h, o, ' ', h, i], args: [f, o, o]
- add_ephemeral_volume: accessModes: [R, e, a, d, W, r, i, t, e, O, n, c, e]

Passing real lists works correctly, for example
secret_names=['my-secret'], command=['echo', 'hi'], access_modes=['ReadWriteOnce'].

### Expected result
A TypeError is raised before compiling when a plain str is passed where a list
of strings is expected. The type hints already say a list is expected
(List[str], and Union[List[str], List[PipelineParameterChannel]] for secret_names).

These are caller mistakes, but they fail silently or only later at pod
creation, so an early TypeError helps users.

### Root cause
Same pattern as #15421. A str is iterable, so it is accepted by loops and
protobuf repeated string fields:
- sdk/python/kfp/kubernetes/image.py:43 (`for secret_name in secret_names`)
- sdk/python/kfp/kubernetes/init_container.py:118-119 (`command`, `args`)
- sdk/python/kfp/kubernetes/volume.py:210 (`access_modes`)

### Open questions
1. Should I follow the approach agreed on #15421 / #15488 (reject a plain str
   with TypeError, and keep lists of PipelineParameterChannel working)?
2. One PR for all three functions, or one PR per function?

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: Experiments fail on, then silently ignore, models that are not battery models
problem_statement.body:
### PyBaMM Version

main

### Python Version

3.13

### Describe the bug

pybamm.Simulation` accepts an experiment with any `pybamm.BaseModel`, but:

1. solving fails at the end of the first cycle, because `pybamm.SummaryVariables` reads `model.summary_variables`, which only `BaseBatteryModel` defines (`BaseModel` initialises `_summary_variables = []` but has no property for it);
2. with that worked around, the steps have no effect on a model that does not read `"Current function [A]"`: every step runs the model with its own parameter values, with no error or warning. A "Rest" and a "Discharge at 1 A" give the same result.

The expected behaviour is that either the experiment controls the model, or `Simulation` raises, saying which step sets a control (`"Current function [A]"`) that the model does not read. Models without summary variables should get an empty cycle summary, not an `AttributeError`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```python3
import pybamm


def heated_body():
    model = pybamm.BaseModel()
    T = pybamm.Variable("Temperature [K]")
    model.rhs = {T: pybamm.Parameter("Heating power [W]") / 1000}
    model.initial_conditions = {T: 300}
    model.variables = {"Temperature [K]": T}
    return model


parameter_values = pybamm.ParameterValues({"Heating power [W]": 100})

sim = pybamm.Simulation(
    heated_body(),
    parameter_values=parameter_values,
    experiment=pybamm.Experiment(["Rest for 10 seconds"]),
)
sim.solve()
# AttributeError: 'BaseModel' object has no attribute 'summary_variables'

for step in ["Rest for 10 seconds", "Discharge at 1 A for 10 seconds"]:
    model = heated_body()
    model.summary_variables = []
    sim = pybamm.Simulation(
        model, parameter_values=parameter_values, experiment=pybamm.Experiment([step])
    )
    print(step, sim.solve()["Temperature [K]"].entries[-1])
# Both print 301.0: the steps had no effect
```

### Relevant log output

```shell
PyBaMM 26.10.0
AttributeError: 'BaseModel' object has no attribute 'summary_variables'
  pybamm/simulation/simulation.py:1195 in solve
  pybamm/solvers/solution.py:1573 in make_cycle_solution
  pybamm/solvers/summary_variable.py:50 in __init__
```

problem_statement.title: v0.3 gRPC client raises A2AClientError for every error from a2a-go's v0.3 server
problem_statement.body:
Against a2a-go's v0.3 gRPC server, every error comes back as a plain `A2AClientError`. Task not found, invalid params, unsupported operation and sending to a finished task all look the same. The v0.3 JSON-RPC client maps them correctly against the same server.

`_map_grpc_error` in `compat/v0_3/grpc_transport.py` only recognizes a status message shaped like `"TaskNotFoundError: ..."`, which is the format a2a-python's own v0.3 server writes. a2a-go sends a plain message and names the error in `ErrorInfo.reason` (`TASK_NOT_FOUND`), the same way the v1 gRPC client already reads it.

```
get_task(missing) -> A2AClientError: gRPC Error NOT_FOUND: failed to get task: task not found
```

problem_statement.title: agent runtime: built-in helpers fail with invalid_tool_arguments (params typed as JSON strings, models send objects)
problem_statement.body:
### Rapid-MLX version

1.0.2 (rapid-mlx --version; bundled runtime of Rapid-MLX Desktop 1.0.2 (196))

### Last version where it worked (if regression)

Unknown. Also reproduced on 1.0.1.

### Hardware

MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Max, 64 GB

### macOS version

macOS 27.3 (26C5035r)

### Python version

3.12.13 (Desktop-bundled); mlx 0.32.3, mlx-lm 0.31.3

### Model

qwen3.5-9b-8bit (mlx-community/Qwen3.5-9B-8bit). Also seen on 1.0.1 with mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit.

### Full serve command

rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-9b-8bit --port 8011

### Streaming or non-streaming?

Non-streaming

### What happened? What did you expect?

Actual: an agent run on /v1/agent/runs with execution: "server" fails on its first model turn with failure_code: "invalid_tool_arguments" and tool_rounds: 0 whenever the model calls one of the two built-in helpers, rapid__calculate or rapid__batch_read_only. This includes the default path: with tool_names omitted, the runtime adds both helpers automatically (as docs/guides/agent-runtime.md describes), the model calls one, and the run fails. In my tests the helpers never ran successfully.

Cause (as far as I can tell): in rapid_mlx/agent_runtime/server.py (v1.0.2), both helpers declare their only argument as a string that should contain JSON:

_CALCULATE_PARAMETERS: "expressions": {"type": "string", ...}. The description says "Pass expressions as a JSON string mapping short result labels to arithmetic strings, for example {"total":"12+8"}".
_BATCH_READ_ONLY_PARAMETERS: "calls": {"type": "string", ...}. "Pass calls as a JSON string containing an array of objects..."
The handlers then json.loads() the string back into a dict or list (_execute_calculator, and the batch handler).

Both models I tried send a real JSON object instead, e.g. {"expressions": {"result": "(17*23)+4"}}. The server's tool-argument schema check then rejects the call with "Tool call 'rapid__calculate' parameter 'expressions' violates declared schema: Expected string, got dict". The agent runtime turns that into invalid_tool_arguments and fails the run.

Control: keeping everything else identical and changing only the declared type of expressions from string to object turns 0/3 valid calls into 3/3 valid calls, for both models I tried. So it does not seem to be a model-capability problem: putting JSON inside a string goes against how these models emit tool calls.

Possibly relevant: the server log shows tool-grammar ... admission=skipped:native_wire_mismatch on these requests. If tool grammar applied here, the model might be constrained to produce a string. I don't know whether that skip is expected for the hermes parser.

Expected: the built-in helpers should be callable by the models the agent runtime supports. Some options (you know the trade-offs better than I do):

Declare the parameters as structured types, e.g. "expressions": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": {"type": "string"}, "minProperties": 1, "maxProperties": 16} and "calls": {"type": "array", "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 8, "items": {...}}, with the handlers accepting the parsed value (optionally still accepting a string, for compatibility).
Or, for these two built-ins only, coerce an object/array into its JSON string before validating (similar in spirit to the coercion discussed in #5692).
Also possibly worth a look, but secondary: a schema-violating argument ends the run on the first turn rather than being returned to the model for a corrected call. That may be intentional; mentioning it in case it isn't.

Test coverage note: in tests/test_agent_server.py the calculator tests construct arguments={"expressions": json.dumps({...})} directly, so they don't exercise what a real model sends through the schema check. A test that feeds a model-style object argument through the validation path would catch this.

Not tested: MiniCPM5-2B (the profile the guide calls measured). It isn't on this machine, so I can't say whether its parser behaves differently.

### Minimal reproduction

Both scripts below need only curl and python3. They are also attached (rapid-mlx-builtin-tool-string-schema.zip).

Start a server with no extra flags:

rapid-mlx serve qwen3.5-9b-8bit --port 8011
Chat-completions repro (same tool name, description and schema as the built-in rapid__calculate; request B changes only the parameter type):

DESC='Calculate up to 16 deterministic arithmetic expressions in one call. Pass expressions as a JSON string mapping short result labels to arithmetic strings, for example {\"total\":\"12+8\"}. Use this for every total, average, difference, percentage, or other arithmetic.'
for T in '{"type":"string","minLength":2,"maxLength":16384}' '{"type":"object","additionalProperties":{"type":"string"}}'; do
  curl -sS -w '\n[HTTP %{http_code}]\n' http://127.0.0.1:8011/v1/chat/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{
      \"model\":\"qwen3.5-9b-8bit\",\"temperature\":0,\"max_tokens\":200,
      \"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Use the calculator tool to compute (17*23)+4.\"}],
      \"tools\":[{\"type\":\"function\",\"function\":{\"name\":\"rapid__calculate\",\"description\":\"$DESC\",
        \"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"expressions\":$T},\"required\":[\"expressions\"],\"additionalProperties\":false}}}]}"
done
Observed:

{"error":{"message":"Tool call 'rapid__calculate' parameter 'expressions' violates declared schema: Expected string, got dict. The model produced a schema-violating argument value; retry with a more constrained prompt or relax the schema.","type":"invalid_request_error","code":null,"param":null}}
[HTTP 400]
{"id":"chatcmpl-5fcabdcb", ... "tool_calls":[{"id":"call_0ccf70c8","type":"function","function":{"name":"rapid__calculate","arguments":"{\"expressions\": {\"result\": \"(17*23)+4\"}}"}}] ...}
[HTTP 200]
Agent-runtime repro (default helpers, no tool_names, no MCP servers):

RID=$(curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8011/v1/agent/runs -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"goal":"Use the calculator tool to compute (17*23)+4 and state the result.","execution":"server","max_tokens":600,"timeout":200,"temperature":0}' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])')
sleep 15
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8011/v1/agent/runs/$RID
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8011/v1/agent/runs/$RID/events
Observed:

{"id":"1abc9168-3ecd-4fba-95c9-2e12190e1f67","model":"qwen3.5-9b-8bit","profile":"qwen3.5-9b","status":"failed","model_turns":1,"tool_rounds":0,"final_synthesis":false,"failure_code":"invalid_tool_arguments","output":null,"pending_action":null}
events: 1 run.created / 2 model.requested (tools=rapid__calculate,rapid__batch_read_only) / 3 run.failed {"code": "invalid_tool_arguments"}
Repeated trials (3 each, temperature 0.3), repro_matrix.py in the attachment:

qwen3.5-9b-8bit  as shipped (string)  #1-3: HTTP 400 ... Expected string, got dict
qwen3.5-9b-8bit  control (object)     #1-3: valid call, expressions is dict: {"result": "(17*23)+4"}
On 1.0.1 the same matrix gave identical results for mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-4bit, and 12/12 agent runs (2 models × 2 goals × 3 trials) failed with invalid_tool_arguments.

[rapid-mlx-builtin-tool-string-schema.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34719273/rapid-mlx-builtin-tool-string-schema.zip)

### Server logs / error output

```shell

# request A (schema as shipped)
INFO:rapid_mlx.routes.chat:[REQUEST] POST /v1/chat/completions stream=False model='qwen3.5-9b-8bit' max_tokens=200 temp=0.0 msgs=1 roles=['user'] total_chars=45 tools=1 response_format=None
INFO:rapid_mlx.routes.chat:tool-grammar request=72358ae670 model='qwen3.5-9b-8bit' admission=skipped:native_wire_mismatch

INFO:     127.0.0.1:60106 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request
# request B (control, type object)
INFO:rapid_mlx.routes.chat:tool-grammar request=72358adfe0 model='qwen3.5-9b-8bit' admission=skipped:native_wire_mismatch
INFO:     127.0.0.1:60112 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
# agent run, execution=server, tool_names omitted
INFO:     127.0.0.1:60114 - "POST /v1/agent/runs HTTP/1.1" 202 Accepted
INFO:rapid_mlx.routes.chat:tool-grammar request=7235a27980 model='qwen3.5-9b-8bit' admission=skipped:native_wire_mismatch
WARNING:rapid_mlx.agent_runtime.server:Agent run 1abc9168-3ecd-4fba-95c9-2e12190e1f67 failed in server adapter (_InvalidToolArgumentsError)
```

problem_statement.title: [question] Recommended approach for warning-as-error missing files in virtual package
problem_statement.body:
### What is your question?

We are successfully building with `core:warnings_as_errors=['*']` for almost everything. We use some virtual packages in the same manner as the [c-c-i opengl virtual package](https://github.com/conan-io/conan-center-index/blob/master/recipes/opengl/all/conanfile.py).

When building opengl or our other virtual packages, we still get the warning promoted to an error of "No files in this package!". What is the recommended approach to be able to address this warning for virtual packages. The idea of creating a dummy file just to silence the warning is a workable kludge but doesn't seem particularly clean.

problem_statement.title: StringLiteral to IntegerType/LongType silently truncates fractional strings, changing predicate meaning
problem_statement.body:
### Apache Iceberg version

0.12.0 (latest release)

### Please describe the bug 🐞

`literal("2.6").to(IntegerType())` returns `LongLiteral(2)` instead of raising, while `DecimalLiteral(Decimal("2.6")).to(IntegerType())` raises ValueError. A bound predicate such as `x < "2.6"` on an int column therefore becomes `x < 2` and wrongly drops rows with x = 2 (verified with `expression_evaluator`); the same bound literal feeds partition pruning, so files can be skipped too.

The sibling `DecimalLiteral.to(IntegerType/LongType)` already rejects fractional values via the existing `_to_integral` helper, with a test spelling out why: rounding would change the predicate (e.g. x > 2.6 becoming x > 3 drops x = 3). The StringLiteral path was missed. The reference Java implementation has no INTEGER/LONG case in `StringLiteral.to()` and refuses the conversion.

Suggested fix: use the existing `_to_integral` helper in both `StringLiteral.to(IntegerType)` and `StringLiteral.to(LongType)`, and update `test_string_literal` to expect ValueError for fractional strings.

Reproduction (pyiceberg 0.12.0, main @ fce8185):
- `literal("2.6").to(IntegerType())` returns `LongLiteral(2)`; same for LongType
- `literal("-2.5").to(IntegerType())` returns `LongLiteral(-2)`; `literal("0.1").to(LongType())` returns `LongLiteral(0)`
- `LessThan("x", "2.6")` bound to an int column becomes `x < 2`, and `expression_evaluator` returns False for a row with x = 2, although x < 2.6 is True
- Integral strings still convert exactly: `literal("2.0").to(IntegerType())` returns 2, `literal("1e3").to(IntegerType())` returns 1000

### Willingness to contribute

- [x] I can contribute a fix for this bug independently
- [ ] I would be willing to contribute a fix for this bug with guidance from the Iceberg community
- [ ] I cannot contribute a fix for this bug at this time

problem_statement.title: [BUG] complete fails for single-column frames with explicit=False and for non-string column labels
problem_statement.body:
Found while reviewing #1834. Both reproduce on `dev` (05fad9bb) with pandas 3.0.5, and neither is introduced by that PR.

## 1. Single-column frame with `explicit=False`

`complete` builds its merge indicator name with `"".join(columns)`, to get a name that is not an existing column. With one column, the joined name is that column's own name, so `merge` rejects it.

```python
import pandas as pd
import janitor

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 3]})
df.complete("a", fill_value=0, explicit=False)
# ValueError: Cannot use name of an existing column for indicator column
```

`explicit=True` and `fill_value=None` both work on the same frame.

## 2. Non-string column labels

Integer labels fail in two different places.

```python
df = pd.DataFrame({0: [1, 2], 1: [1, 2], 2: [1.0, None]})

df.complete(0, 1)
# ValueError: Kindly ensure the Series at position 0 has a name.
# Same error with fill_value=0, with explicit=True or False.

df.complete([0], [1], fill_value=0, explicit=False)
# TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, int found
```

The first error comes from the `expand` step and happens even without `fill_value`. The second comes from the same `"".join(columns)` as in item 1, so it needs a fix of its own once `expand` accepts such labels. The code comment in `complete` says the fill loop was written to cater for non-string column names, so non-string labels look intended to work.

## Suggested direction

- Replace `"".join(columns)` with a guaranteed-unused indicator name, for example a fresh sentinel string or `object()`-based label that is checked against `df.columns`.
- Decide whether non-string labels are supported by `complete` and `expand`. If so, fix the label handling in `expand`. If not, raise a clear error.

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: cloudpaw plugin fails to load on Chinese Windows (legacy_cloudpaw.py reads JSON without an explicit encoding)
problem_statement.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (pip install). The same code is on `main` as of `f47dd19b`.

## Description

On Chinese Windows (system ANSI code page = `cp936` / GBK) the built-in `cloudpaw` plugin fails to load at all.

`src/qwenpaw/plugins/legacy_cloudpaw.py` reads three kinds of JSON file — the uninstall marker, `workspaces/<agent>/agent.json`, and the skill pool `skill.json` — with `Path.read_text()` and **no explicit `encoding`**, so Python falls back to the process locale encoding. QwenPaw itself writes those files as UTF-8, so any `agent.json` that contains CJK text raises `UnicodeDecodeError` while the loader imports the module, and the plugin is marked as failed.

`loader.py` reports this as a generic "plugin failed to load", so nothing in the message points at the code page and the user has no way to know why.

The file is inconsistent with itself: line 30 already pins `encoding="utf-8"`; seven other reads do not:

| Line | Expression | File read |
|-----:|------------|-----------|
| 83 | `json.loads(_marker().read_text())` | uninstall marker |
| 142 | `json.loads(path.read_text())` | uninstall marker |
| 159 | `json.loads(agent_file.read_text())` | `workspaces/<agent>/agent.json` |
| 182 | `json.loads(manifest.read_text())` | `<skill pool>/skill.json` |
| 240 | `json.loads(_marker().read_text())` | uninstall marker |
| 347 | `json.loads(profile_path.read_text())` | `workspaces/<agent>/agent.json` |
| 364 | `json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())` | `<skill pool>/skill.json` |

**Related PR(s):** opening right after this issue.

**Security considerations:** none — this is a decoding failure, not a disclosure.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 (and `main` at `f47dd19b`)
- **OS:** Windows Server 2022 (AMD64); also seen on Windows 11
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12
- **Locale:** `locale.getencoding()` returns `cp936`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use Windows with a Chinese system locale, so `locale.getencoding()` returns `cp936`.
2. Have an agent whose `workspaces/<agent>/agent.json` contains CJK text. QwenPaw writes that file as UTF-8, so any Chinese agent name is enough.
3. Start QwenPaw and let the loader import `cloudpaw`.

The underlying mechanics, reproducible anywhere:

```python
import json
blob = json.dumps({"name": "药老"}, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
blob.decode("gbk")   # UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x80 ...
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** plugin load aborts and the plugin is marked failed; `cloudpaw` is unusable on every Chinese Windows install that has a CJK agent name.
- **Expected:** the plugin loads, because the JSON it reads was written by QwenPaw as UTF-8.

```
ERROR  plugin 'cloudpaw' failed to load
  File "...\qwenpaw\plugins\legacy_cloudpaw.py", line 159, in remember
    profile = json.loads(agent_file.read_text())
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 137:
                     illegal multibyte sequence
```

## Logs / Screenshots

See the traceback above. `loader.py` surfaces only `plugin 'cloudpaw' failed to load` plus that traceback; the byte offset (`position 137`) lands in the middle of a multi-byte character that was valid UTF-8, which is the giveaway.

## Additional Notes

This cannot be caught by CI as it stands, and it is worth knowing why: `Path.read_text()` delegates to `io.open()`, which resolves `encoding=None` through the **C-level** locale encoding. Patching `locale.getencoding()` from Python does not change it, so a UTF-8 CI runner cannot be turned into a failing one by monkeypatching. A regression test therefore has to assert the encoding contract rather than depend on the locale — which is what the PR does.

Workarounds for affected users are all unpleasant: enable *Region → Administrative → Change system locale → Beta: Use Unicode UTF-8 for worldwide language support*, or strip non-ASCII characters out of `agent.json`.

+    maintenance_work: SimpleNamespace,
+):
+    """On Postgres every vacuum task draws on the one-connection maintenance
+    pool, so a worker with spare capacity must still run them one at a time."""
+    async with Docket(name=f"test-db-vacuum-{uuid.uuid4()}", url="memory://") as docket:
+        for task in VACUUM_TASKS:
+            docket.register(task)
+
+        await schedule_vacuum_tasks(docket=docket)
+        await schedule_event_vacuum_tasks(docket=docket)
+        await schedule_orphan_vacuum_tasks(docket=docket)
+
+        async with Worker(docket, concurrency=len(VACUUM_TASKS)) as worker:
+            await worker.run_until_finished()
+
+    assert maintenance_work.max_active == 1
+    assert maintenance_work.ran == {task.__name__ for task in VACUUM_TASKS}
+
+
+async def test_vacuum_tasks_all_run_once_after_a_hold_across_scheduler_cycles(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
+):
+    """The schedulers run on different loops, so one can fire again while a
+    vacuum task holds the slot. Once the holder finishes, every waiting task
+    must run without another scheduler cycle, each once, one at a time."""
+    holder: list[str] = []
+    release_holder = asyncio.Event()
+    executions: dict[str, set[int]] = {}
+    active = 0
+    max_active = 0
+
+    async def hold_maintenance_connection() -> None:
+        nonlocal active, max_active
+        execution = current_execution.get()
+        active += 1
+        max_active = max(max_active, active)
+        try:
+            if not holder:
+                holder.append(execution.key)
+                await release_holder.wait()
+            executions.setdefault(execution.key, set()).add(execution.generation)
+        finally:
+            active -= 1
+
+    _stub_maintenance_helpers(monkeypatch, hold_maintenance_connection)
+
+    async def wait_until_parked(docket: Docket, keys: set[str]) -> None:
+        async for attempt in retry_asserts(max_attempts=100, delay=0.05):
+            with attempt:
+                for key in keys:
+                    execution = await docket.get_execution(key)
+                    assert execution is not None
+                    assert execution.state is ExecutionState.SCHEDULED
+
+    async with Docket(name=f"test-db-vacuum-{uuid.uuid4()}", url="memory://") as docket:
+        for task in VACUUM_TASKS:
+            docket.register(task)
+
+        async with Worker(docket, concurrency=len(VACUUM_TASKS)) as worker:
+            worker_loop = asyncio.create_task(worker.run_forever())
+            try:
+                await schedule_vacuum_tasks(docket=docket)
+                async for attempt in retry_asserts(max_attempts=100, delay=0.05):
+                    with attempt:
+                        assert holder == ["db-vacuum:old-flow-runs"]
+
+                event_keys = {"db-vacuum:retention-overrides", "db-vacuum:old-events"}
+                await schedule_event_vacuum_tasks(docket=docket)
+                await wait_until_parked(docket, event_keys)
+                await schedule_event_vacuum_tasks(docket=docket)
+                await schedule_orphan_vacuum_tasks(docket=docket)
+                await wait_until_parked(docket, set(VACUUM_TASK_KEYS) - set(holder))
+                release_holder.set()
+
+                async for attempt in retry_asserts(max_attempts=200, delay=0.05):
+                    with attempt:
+                        assert set(executions) == set(VACUUM_TASK_KEYS)
+            finally:
+                worker_loop.cancel()
+                await asyncio.gather(worker_loop, return_exceptions=True)
+
+    assert {key: len(generations) for key, generations in executions.items()} == {
+        key: 1 for key in VACUUM_TASK_KEYS
+    }
+    assert max_active == 1
+
+
+def _released_vacuum_task(
+    task: Callable[..., Awaitable[None]], ran: set[str]
+) -> Callable[..., Awaitable[None]]:
+    """A vacuum task with the signature released servers registered, which has
+    no parameter beyond the injected database interface."""
+
+    async def released_task(*, db: object = None) -> None:
+        ran.add(task.__name__)
+
+    released_task.__name__ = task.__name__
+    return released_task
+
+
+async def test_released_worker_runs_calls_from_the_vacuum_schedulers():
+    """During a rolling upgrade, a worker that is still on a released version
+    can claim the calls that upgraded schedulers enqueue."""
+    name = f"test-db-vacuum-{uuid.uuid4()}"
+    url = f"memory://{name}"
+    ran: set[str] = set()
+
+    async with Docket(name=name, url=url) as upgraded_server:
+        await schedule_vacuum_tasks(docket=upgraded_server)
+        await schedule_event_vacuum_tasks(docket=upgraded_server)
+        await schedule_orphan_vacuum_tasks(docket=upgraded_server)
+
+        async with Docket(name=name, url=url) as released_server:
+            for task in VACUUM_TASKS:
+                released_server.register(_released_vacuum_task(task, ran))
+
+            async with Worker(
+                released_server, concurrency=len(VACUUM_TASKS)
+            ) as released_worker:
+                await released_worker.run_until_finished()
+
+    assert ran == {task.__name__ for task in VACUUM_TASKS}
+
+
+async def test_upgraded_worker_runs_calls_from_a_released_server_one_at_a_time(
+    maintenance_work: SimpleNamespace,
+):
+    """During a rolling upgrade, a worker that has upgraded can claim the calls
+    a released scheduler enqueued, and those calls still share the slot."""
+    name = f"test-db-vacuum-{uuid.uuid4()}"
+    url = f"memory://{name}"
+
+    async with Docket(name=name, url=url) as released_server:
+        for task in VACUUM_TASKS:
+            await released_server.add(
+                _released_vacuum_task(task, set()), key=f"db-vacuum:{task.__name__}"
+            )()
+
+        async with Docket(name=name, url=url) as upgraded_server:
+            for task in VACUUM_TASKS:
+                upgraded_server.register(task)
+
+            async with Worker(
+                upgraded_server, concurrency=len(VACUUM_TASKS)
+            ) as upgraded_worker:
+                await upgraded_worker.run_until_finished()
+
+    assert maintenance_work.max_active == 1
+    assert maintenance_work.ran == {task.__name__ for task in VACUUM_TASKS}
+
+
 class TestVacuumOrphanedLogs:
     async def test_deletes_orphaned_logs(self, session, flow):
         """Logs referencing a non-existent flow run should be deleted."""

problem_statement.title: `db_vacuum` Docket jobs run concurrently against a size-1 maintenance pool and time out hourly
problem_statement.body:
## Bug summary

On a self-hosted Prefect server backed by PostgreSQL, the hourly `db_vacuum`
jobs are enqueued as separate Docket tasks and execute concurrently, but all of
them share a dedicated maintenance SQLAlchemy pool with `pool_size=1` and
`max_overflow=0`.

When one vacuum query holds that single connection for longer than 30 seconds,
the sibling jobs fail together with pool-checkout timeouts instead of waiting
for the maintenance work to run sequentially:

```text
sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 1 overflow 0 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00
```

We have directly observed this every hour in production since upgrading to
Prefect 3.7.5. A recent burst on 2026-08-23 contained five failures:

```text
12:16:40.033 | ERROR | docket.worker - [30003ms] vacuum_orphaned_artifacts(){db-vacuum:orphaned-artifacts}
12:16:40.044 | ERROR | docket.worker - [30012ms] vacuum_stale_artifact_collections(){db-vacuum:stale-collections}
12:16:40.051 | ERROR | docket.worker - [30018ms] vacuum_old_flow_runs(){db-vacuum:old-flow-runs}
12:16:41.705 | ERROR | docket.worker - [30003ms] vacuum_events_with_retention_overrides(){db-vacuum:retention-overrides}
12:16:41.713 | ERROR | docket.worker - [30009ms] vacuum_old_events(){db-vacuum:old-events}
```

Each entry ends with the same `QueuePool` timeout. A representative traceback
tail is:

```text
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/docket/worker.py", line 1029, in _execute
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/prefect/server/services/db_vacuum.py", line 329, in vacuum_old_events
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/prefect/server/services/db_vacuum.py", line 442, in _batch_delete
    result = await session.execute(...)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/session.py", line 2113, in _connection_for_bind
    return trans._connection_for_bind(engine, execution_options)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 3295, in connect
    return self._connection_cls(self)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/base.py", line 3319, in raw_connection
    return self.pool.connect()
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/sqlalchemy/pool/base.py", line 448, in connect
    return _ConnectionFairy._checkout(self)
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/sqlalchemy/pool/impl.py", line 167, in _do_get
    raise exc.TimeoutError(...)
sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 1 overflow 0 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00
```

### Reproduction conditions

1. Run a self-hosted Prefect server with PostgreSQL.
2. Enable flow-run vacuum with
   `PREFECT_SERVER_SERVICES_DB_VACUUM_ENABLED=true`; event vacuum is enabled by
   default.
3. Have enough retained data that one hourly vacuum job holds its connection
   for more than 30 seconds.
4. At the hourly vacuum boundary, observe the separately enqueued Docket jobs
   start together. One obtains the maintenance connection and the others fail
   after approximately 30 seconds.

The source appears to explain the behavior:

- [`_maintenance_database_config`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/3.8.3/src/prefect/server/services/db_vacuum.py#L59-L79)
  caches one maintenance configuration per connection URL and hard-codes the
  pool to size 1 / overflow 0. Its comment says this is safe because vacuum
  tasks run sequentially.
- [`schedule_vacuum_tasks`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/3.8.3/src/prefect/server/services/db_vacuum.py#L114-L145)
  and
  [`schedule_event_vacuum_tasks`](https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/blob/3.8.3/src/prefect/server/services/db_vacuum.py#L148-L174)
  enqueue the cleanup functions as separate Docket tasks on automatic hourly
  schedules.
- The background Docket worker can execute those jobs concurrently, so the
  source comment's sequential-execution assumption does not hold.

The same code is still present in the 3.8.3 tag and current `main`; however, our
runtime observation is from 3.7.5.

Expected behavior: `db_vacuum` jobs sharing the one-connection maintenance pool
should be serialized or protected by a concurrency limit so they eventually all
run. Merely increasing the pool size may allow concurrent delete work and
reintroduce deadlock pressure, so serialization seems safer.

## Version info

```text
Version:              3.7.5
API version:          0.8.4
Python version:       3.13
Git commit:           756685ab
OS/Arch:              linux/amd64
Server type:          server
Database:             PostgreSQL
Pydantic version:     2.12.5
Container image:      prefect:3.7.5-python3.13
```

## Additional context

This does not appear to be global PostgreSQL connection exhaustion: during
sampled bursts, total database connection use remained low and API requests
continued succeeding. The contention is isolated to the dedicated maintenance
engine introduced by #22291.

Disabling the optional flow-run vacuum family reduces the number of competing
jobs but does not eliminate contention between the event-vacuum jobs. Disabling
all vacuum work avoids the error at the cost of unbounded retention, so it is
not a durable workaround.

problem_statement.title: [BUG] FFT never aligns weekly seasonality: `"weekday"` resolves to a method on `pd.Timestamp`
problem_statement.body:
## Descripción

**Describe the bug**

When `FFT` detects weekly seasonality (daily series, or hourly series with a weekly pattern), `_find_relevant_timestamp_attributes()` returns `{"weekday"}` (`darts/models/forecasting/fft.py`, lines 117 and 127). `_compare_timestamps_on_attributes()` then compares `getattr(ts_1, "weekday") == getattr(ts_2, "weekday")`, but on a `pd.Timestamp`, `weekday` is a **method**, not a property. Two bound methods of different timestamps never compare equal, even when both dates fall on the same day of the week, so `_crop_to_match_seasons()` never finds a matching timestamp. It logs `"No matching timestamp could be found, returning original TimeSeries."` and fits on the uncropped series, so the weekly seasonal phase is not aligned with the forecast start.

The same happens when a user passes `required_matches={"weekday"}`.

**To Reproduce**

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from darts import TimeSeries
from darts.models import FFT

idx = pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=73, freq="D")
pattern = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 12], dtype=float)
ts = TimeSeries.from_times_and_values(idx, np.tile(pattern, 11)[: len(idx)])
truth = np.roll(pattern, -(len(idx) % 7))

for required_matches in [None, {"day_of_week"}]:
    model = FFT(required_matches=required_matches)
    model.fit(ts)
    pred = model.predict(7).values().ravel()
    print(required_matches, "MAE:", np.abs(pred - truth).mean())
```

Output (darts `master`, pandas 3.1.0):

```text
No matching timestamp could be found, returning original TimeSeries.
None MAE: 3.687
{'day_of_week'} MAE: 1.94
```

```python
>>> a, b = pd.Timestamp("2024-01-01"), pd.Timestamp("2024-01-08")  # both Mondays
>>> getattr(a, "weekday") == getattr(b, "weekday")
False
>>> getattr(a, "day_of_week") == getattr(b, "day_of_week")
True
```

**Expected behavior**

With the default `required_matches=None`, weekly seasonality is detected and the training series is cropped to match the day of the week of the first prediction point.

**Proposed fix**

Use the `day_of_week` property instead of `"weekday"` in `_find_relevant_timestamp_attributes()` (lines 117 and 127), and update the `test_fft.py` expectations accordingly. Optionally, `_compare_timestamps_on_attributes()` could raise a clear error if an attribute in `required_matches` is not a property (e.g. callable), so that user-provided `required_matches={"weekday"}` doesn't fail silently.

I'd be happy to open a PR for this.

**System:**
- Python version: 3.13
- darts version: `master` (0.48.1)

problem_statement.title: [Bug]: message/send hangs forever when the AgentExecutor returns without producing events
problem_statement.body:
### What happened? `message/send` **hangs indefinitely** when an `AgentExecutor` returns normally without enqueueing any event. Both handlers are affected: - `DefaultRequestHandlerV2`: no response within 3s (tested; it never returns). - `DefaultRequestHandler` (legacy): no response within 10s (tested; it never returns), even though it contains an `if not result: raise InternalError` guard at `src/a2a/server/request_handlers/default_request_handler.py:456-457` — empirically that line is never reached in this scenario. Each hanging request pins a client connection plus the handler's internal producer/consumer tasks. ### Root cause (V2) `default_request_handler_v2.py:437-439`: ```python if result is None: logger.debug('Missing result for task %s', request_context.task_id) result = await active_task.get_task() ``` `ActiveTask.get_task()` (`src/a2a/server/agent_execution/active_task.py:965-967`) awaits `self._task_created.wait()` with **no timeout**. `_task_created` is only set when (a) the task already existed at `start()`, (b) the consumer processes a task event, or (c) the producer fails. A *silent success* (executor returns, zero events) sets none of them, so the wait never completes. For the legacy handler, the equivalent `raise InternalError` guard exists but is unreachable in this scenario — the flow blocks earlier inside `consume_and_break_on_interrupt`. ### Reproduction
Self-contained script (main @ 494a8ec, Python 3.10) ```python import asyncio from a2a.auth.user import UnauthenticatedUser from a2a.server.agent_execution import AgentExecutor from a2a.server.context import ServerCallContext from a2a.server.request_handlers import DefaultRequestHandlerV2 from a2a.server.tasks import InMemoryTaskStore from a2a.types.a2a_pb2 import ( AgentCapabilities, AgentCard, Message, Part, Role, SendMessageConfiguration, SendMessageRequest, ) class SilentExecutor(AgentExecutor): # Returns normally without producing any event. The AgentExecutor # contract only says it *should* enqueue events, so this is a legal # (if buggy) implementation. async def execute(self, context, event_queue): return None async def cancel(self, context, event_queue): pass async def main(): handler = DefaultRequestHandlerV2( agent_executor=SilentExecutor(), task_store=InMemoryTaskStore(), agent_card=AgentCard( name='t', version='1.0', capabilities=AgentCapabilities(streaming=True), ), ) params = SendMessageRequest( message=Message( role=Role.ROLE_USER, message_id='m1', parts=[Part(text='Hi')] ), configuration=SendMessageConfiguration( accepted_output_modes=['text/plain'] ), ) try: await asyncio.wait_for( handler.on_message_send( params, ServerCallContext(user=UnauthenticatedUser()) ), timeout=3, ) print('returned (no hang)') except asyncio.TimeoutError: print('HANG CONFIRMED: on_message_send did not return within 3s') asyncio.run(main()) ```
Observed output: ```text HANG CONFIRMED: on_message_send did not return within 3s ``` ### Expected behavior `message/send` should fail fast with an `InternalError` (as the legacy handler's `raise InternalError` guard intends) when the agent produces no result at all, instead of hanging forever and leaking the request, producer and consumer tasks. ### Suggested fix - In `DefaultRequestHandlerV2.on_message_send`, when `result is None` and `_task_created` is not set, raise `InternalError` instead of awaiting `get_task()` (aligning with the legacy guard's intent). Alternatively, add a timeout to `ActiveTask.get_task()`. - Worth auditing why the legacy handler never reaches its `raise InternalError` guard in this scenario. Happy to submit a PR with tests. ### Relevant log output ```text HANG CONFIRMED: on_message_send did not return within 3s ``` ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

problem_statement.title: [BUG] SolverVBD: dihedral bending is silently off for hinges with triangles smaller than ~1 mm (absolute degeneracy threshold)
problem_statement.body:
### Bug Description

`evaluate_dihedral_angle_based_bending_force_hessian` treats a hinge as degenerate and returns zero force and Hessian when ([`particle_vbd_kernels.py:716`](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/0679304388f3edfea6e7e942232724425d089cd3/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/particle_vbd_kernels.py#L716), [L736-L745](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/0679304388f3edfea6e7e942232724425d089cd3/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/particle_vbd_kernels.py#L736-L745)):

```python
eps = 1.0e-6
n1 = wp.cross(x02, x03)
n2 = wp.cross(x13, x12)
...
if n1_norm < eps or n2_norm < eps or e_norm < eps:
    return wp.vec3(0.0), wp.mat33(0.0)
```

`n1` and `n2` are not normalized: their length is twice the triangle area in m^2. The test is therefore `area < 5e-7 m^2`, an absolute size, not a shape test. On a right-triangle grid every hinge with legs below 1 mm is skipped, without a warning, so cloth meshed finer than about 1 mm has membrane forces but no bending at all, whatever `edge_ke` is. The damping term repeats the same test on the previous positions ([L825](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/blob/0679304388f3edfea6e7e942232724425d089cd3/newton/_src/solvers/vbd/particle_vbd_kernels.py#L825)).

From the script below (main, CPU):

- a hinge folded 30 degrees gets the same force (0.5236 N for `edge_ke` 1) for legs of 10, 2, 1.2 and 1 mm, as it should (the force does not depend on the scale), and exactly 0 for legs of 0.8 and 0.5 mm;
- a strip clamped at one end, 28 x 14 cells: with 5 mm cells, raising `edge_ke` from 1e-4 to 100 lifts the tip from -132.6 to -107.8 mm after 0.2 s; with 0.5 mm cells, `edge_ke` 1e-4 and 1 give bitwise identical positions.

**Expected.** A hinge is degenerate when its triangles are degenerate in shape (height much smaller than the edge), independent of the mesh scale. Sub-millimetre meshes (fine cloth, thin films, small parts) get bending forces that scale with `edge_ke`.

**Proposed fix.** Compare the unnormalized normals with `eps` times the squared edge length, in both places:

```python
area_eps = eps * e_norm * e_norm
if e_norm < eps or n1_norm < area_eps or n2_norm < area_eps:
    return wp.vec3(0.0), wp.mat33(0.0)
```

A triangle then counts as degenerate when its height is below `1e-6` times the edge, which is what the current test does for 1 m edges. With this change the script gives 0.5236 N for every hinge size, the 0.5 mm strip's tip rises from -13.8 to -5.5 mm when `edge_ke` goes from 1e-4 to 1, and the 5 mm strip is unchanged. I can open a PR with this change and a regression test.

### Reproduction Script

```python
"""SolverVBD dihedral bending: hinges whose triangles are smaller than ~1 mm get no bending force.

usage: python repro.py [cpu|cuda:0]
1. One hinge (two right triangles with legs L sharing an edge), folded 30 degrees from its flat rest angle: bending
   force on an opposite vertex for several L. The energy is 0.5 * edge_ke * rest_length * theta^2 and d(theta)/dx
   scales with 1/L, so the force does not depend on L.
2. A strip clamped at one end, under gravity, the same mesh at two scales: tip height after 0.2 s for two
   values of edge_ke (1e-4 and a stiff value).
"""

import sys

import numpy as np
import warp as wp

import newton
from newton._src.solvers.vbd.particle_vbd_kernels import evaluate_dihedral_angle_based_bending_force_hessian

wp.config.log_level = wp.LOG_WARNING
DEVICE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "cpu"


@wp.kernel
def hinge_force(pos: wp.array[wp.vec3], edges: wp.array2d[wp.int32], rest_angle: wp.array[float],
                rest_length: wp.array[float], out: wp.array[wp.vec3]):
    f, h = evaluate_dihedral_angle_based_bending_force_hessian(0, 0, pos, pos, edges, rest_angle, rest_length,
                                                               1.0, 0.0, 1.0e-3)
    out[0] = f


def hinge_check():
    print("1. hinge folded 30 deg, edge_ke 1 N, force on opposite vertex 0:")
    a = np.radians(30.0)
    for L in (1.0e-2, 2.0e-3, 1.2e-3, 1.0e-3, 8.0e-4, 5.0e-4):
        # edge from x2 = (0, 0, 0) to x3 = (L, 0, 0); opposite vertices at distance L from the edge
        x = np.array([[0.0, L * np.cos(a), L * np.sin(a)], [0.0, -L, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [L, 0.0, 0.0]])
        pos = wp.array(x.astype(np.float32), dtype=wp.vec3, device=DEVICE)
        edges = wp.array(np.array([[0, 1, 2, 3]], np.int32), dtype=wp.int32, device=DEVICE)
        out = wp.zeros(1, dtype=wp.vec3, device=DEVICE)
        wp.launch(hinge_force, dim=1, inputs=[pos, edges, wp.array([0.0], dtype=float, device=DEVICE),
                                              wp.array([L], dtype=float, device=DEVICE)], outputs=[out], device=DEVICE)
        print(f"   L = {L * 1e3:5.2f} mm (2 x triangle area {L * L:.2e} m^2): |f| = {np.linalg.norm(out.numpy()[0]):.4f} N")


def strip_tip(cell, edge_ke, nx=28, ny=14, seconds=0.2, dt=1.0e-3):
    b = newton.ModelBuilder()
    b.add_cloth_grid(pos=wp.vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), rot=wp.quat_identity(), vel=wp.vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), dim_x=nx, dim_y=ny,
                     cell_x=cell, cell_y=cell, mass=0.02 * cell * cell, fix_left=True, tri_ke=1.0e3, tri_ka=1.0e3,
                     tri_kd=0.0, edge_ke=edge_ke, edge_kd=0.0, particle_radius=0.1 * cell)
    b.color()
    m = b.finalize(device=DEVICE)
    solver = newton.solvers.SolverVBD(m, iterations=10)
    s0, s1, control = m.state(), m.state(), m.control()
    for _ in range(int(round(seconds / dt))):
        s0.clear_forces()
        solver.step(s0, s1, control, None, dt)
        s0, s1 = s1, s0
    q = s0.particle_q.numpy()
    return q[:, 2].min() - 1.0, q


def strip_check():
    print("2. strip clamped at one end (28 x 14 cells, 20 g/m^2, tri_ke 1e3), gravity, tip height after 0.2 s:")
    for cell, stiff in ((5.0e-3, 100.0), (5.0e-4, 1.0)):    # a stiff value each mesh still steps stably
        (za, qa), (zb, qb) = strip_tip(cell, 1.0e-4), strip_tip(cell, stiff)
        print(f"   cell {cell * 1e3:.1f} mm: edge_ke 1e-4: {za * 1e3:8.3f} mm, edge_ke {stiff:g}: {zb * 1e3:8.3f} mm, "
              f"identical positions: {np.array_equal(qa, qb)}")


print(f"newton {newton.__version__}, warp {wp.__version__}, device {DEVICE}")
hinge_check()
strip_check()
```

Output on `main` (06793043), CPU:

```
newton 1.8.0.dev0, warp 1.18.0, device cpu
1. hinge folded 30 deg, edge_ke 1 N, force on opposite vertex 0:
   L = 10.00 mm (2 x triangle area 1.00e-04 m^2): |f| = 0.5236 N
   L =  2.00 mm (2 x triangle area 4.00e-06 m^2): |f| = 0.5236 N
   L =  1.20 mm (2 x triangle area 1.44e-06 m^2): |f| = 0.5236 N
   L =  1.00 mm (2 x triangle area 1.00e-06 m^2): |f| = 0.5236 N
   L =  0.80 mm (2 x triangle area 6.40e-07 m^2): |f| = 0.0000 N
   L =  0.50 mm (2 x triangle area 2.50e-07 m^2): |f| = 0.0000 N
2. strip clamped at one end (28 x 14 cells, 20 g/m^2, tri_ke 1e3), gravity, tip height after 0.2 s:
   cell 5.0 mm: edge_ke 1e-4: -132.573 mm, edge_ke 100: -107.754 mm, identical positions: False
   cell 0.5 mm: edge_ke 1e-4:  -13.764 mm, edge_ke 1:  -13.764 mm, identical positions: True
```

CUDA (L4) gives the same hinge forces, and with 0.5 mm cells both `edge_ke` values again give identical positions (tip -13.630 mm).

### System Information

- Newton: main @ 06793043 (1.8.0.dev0)
- Warp: 1.18.0
- Python: 3.12.15
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
- GPU: none for the run above; the CUDA run used an NVIDIA L4 (driver 580.178.04)

title: fix: parse negative numbers as positionals when the command has **kwargs
issue_title: **kwargs captures negative-number positionals (e.g. -5) as keywords, silently corrupting args

problem_statement.title: **kwargs captures negative-number positionals (e.g. -5) as keywords, silently corrupting args
problem_statement.body:
`**kwargs` is documented as consuming tokens "starting with `--`"
(docs: Args & Kwargs), but single-hyphen tokens are also captured, including
negative numbers intended as positional values.

```python
from cyclopts import App
app = App(result_action="return_value")

@app.default
def main(*nums: int, **opts: str):
    return nums, opts

print(app(["-5", "-6"]))            # ((), {'5': '-6'})  <- expected ((-5, -6), {})
print(app(["-1", "2"]))             # ((), {'1': '2'})
app(["-1"], exit_on_error=False)    # MissingArgumentError: Parameter -1 requires an argument.
print(app(["--", "-1", "2"]))       # ((-1, 2), {})  works with "--"
```

The same function without `**opts` parses `["-5", "-6"]` as `(-5, -6)`.

**Cause:** `Argument.match` for a VAR_KEYWORD argument does
`term.lstrip("-")`, so `-1` matches as keyword `"1"`.

**Environment:** cyclopts <YOUR VERSION>, Python <YOUR VERSION>, <YOUR OS>.

I have a small fix that makes negative numbers/slices not match the catch-all
(plain `-x` still goes to kwargs, so nothing else changes); the full test suite
passes. Happy to open a PR with a regression test if the direction is right.
