+    assert source.chk_start_idx.tolist() == starts
+    assert source.chk_end_idx.tolist() == ends
+    assert len(source.timeaxis) == 27
+
+
+@pytest.mark.aqua
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "savefreq, timestep, start, end, timestyle, expected_starts, expected_ends",
+    [
+        ("6h", "h", "20240101T0600", "20240104T0600", "step", [6, 78], [72, 78]),
+        ("MS", "MS", "20240101", "20250101", "yearmonth", [0, 12], [11, 12]),
+        ("MS", "h", "20240101", "20250101", "step", [0, 8784], [8040, 8784]),
+    ],
+)
+def test_integer_chunks_count_saved_frames_not_native_steps(
+    fdb_source_factory, savefreq, timestep, start, end, timestyle, expected_starts, expected_ends
+):
+    """Twelve frames must span 72 hours for six-hourly data and twelve calendar months for monthly data."""
+    _, make_source = fdb_source_factory
+    source = make_source(
+        chunks={"time": 12}, savefreq=savefreq, timestep=timestep, startdate=start, enddate=end, timestyle=timestyle
+    )
+    assert source.chk_size.tolist() == [12, 1]
+    assert source.chk_start_idx.tolist() == expected_starts
+    assert source.chk_end_idx.tolist() == expected_ends
+    assert len(source.timeaxis) == 13
+
+
+@pytest.mark.aqua
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("chunks", [0, -1, True, False])
+def test_integer_time_chunks_reject_invalid_counts(fdb_source_factory, chunks):
+    """Invalid counts must raise a clear error instead of failing in upper() or grouping."""
+    _, make_source = fdb_source_factory
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Time chunk size must be a positive integer"):
+        make_source(chunks={"time": chunks}, startdate="20240101", enddate="20240102")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.aqua
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("chunks", [12, 13])
+def test_integer_chunks_preserve_bridge_alignment_checks(fdb_source_factory, chunks):
+    """A chunk must not silently retrieve frames from two different FDB stores."""
+    _, make_source = fdb_source_factory
+    kwargs = {
+        "chunks": chunks,
+        "startdate": "20240101",
+        "enddate": "20240101T2300",
+        "bridge_start_date": "20240101T1200",
+        "bridge_end_date": "20240101T2300",
+    }
+    if chunks == 13:
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Chunk size is not aligned"):
+            make_source(**kwargs)
+    else:
+        source = make_source(**kwargs)
+        assert source.chk_size.tolist() == [12, 12]
+        assert source.chk_type.tolist() == [0, 1]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.aqua
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("method", ["read", "to_dask"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "freq, start, end, timestyle",
+    [("h", "20240101T0000", "20240102T0200", "date"), ("MS", "20240101", "20250101", "yearmonth")],
+)
+def test_integer_chunks_read_aligned_frames(fdb_source_factory, monkeypatch, freq, start, end, timestyle, method):
+    """Aligned integer chunks must retrieve each saved frame once with the declared Dask chunk sizes."""
+    module, make_source = fdb_source_factory
+    dates = pd.date_range("20240101", "20251231", freq=freq)
+    data = xr.Dataset({"2t": ("time", range(len(dates)), {"GRIB_paramId": 167})}, coords={"time": dates})
+
+    def selected(value):
+        bounds = str(value).split("/to/")
+        return range(int(bounds[0]), int(bounds[-1]) + 1)
+
+    class Retriever:
+        def __init__(self, **kwargs):
+            pass
+
+        def request_data(self, request, **kwargs):
+            time = data.time.dt
+            if "year" in request:
+                mask = time.year.isin(selected(request["year"])) & time.month.isin(selected(request["month"]))
+            else:
+                mask = time.strftime("%Y%m%d").astype(int).isin(selected(request["date"]))
+                mask &= time.strftime("%H%M").astype(int).isin(selected(request["time"]))
+            return data.sel(time=mask)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(module, "GSVRetriever", Retriever, raising=False)
+    source = make_source(chunks={"time": 12}, startdate=start, enddate=end, savefreq=freq, timestep=freq, timestyle=timestyle)
+    result = getattr(source, method)()
+    if method == "to_dask":
+        assert result["2t"].chunksizes["time"] == ((12, 12, 3) if freq == "h" else (12, 1))
+    xr.testing.assert_equal(result, data.sel(time=slice(pd.Timestamp(start), pd.Timestamp(end))))

problem_statement.title: [FDB] Integer time chunks fail in GSV and Polytope engines
problem_statement.body:
### machine

Not specified; the failure occurs in backend-independent partition planning.

### catalog

Any FDB-backed source using the GSV or Polytope engine.

### version

Current development version (main).

### What happened?

Running an analysis with `reader_kwargs: {chunks: {"time": 12}}` fails with `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'upper'` in `FDBSource._compute_partition_plan()`.

The intended meaning is 12 saved time steps per chunk, consistent with the NetCDF driver and the z3fdb engine. The GSV and Polytope engines instead assume that time chunking is a pandas frequency string and call `.upper()` on the integer without validation. Intake and Reader forward the value unchanged.

Guarding `.upper()` alone is insufficient: `_compute_timeaxis()` later passes the same integer to pandas `resample()`, which expects a frequency.

Expected: positive integer time chunks group consecutive saved frames, with a smaller final chunk when necessary. Counts should work independently of save frequency, including monthly data. Existing frequency strings and the `S` single-frame default should retain their behavior, and invalid counts should raise a clear error.

### Code to reproduce the issue

```yaml
reader_kwargs:
  chunks:
    time: 12
```

Equivalent Python for an existing FDB catalog source:

```python
reader = Reader(model=..., exp=..., source=..., engine="gsv", chunks={"time": 12})
data = reader.retrieve()
```

The same shared planner is used by `engine="polytope"`.

### Error messages

```text
if chunking_time.upper() == "S":
AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'upper'
```

### Are you interested in making a pull request?

Yes.

problem_statement.body:
### Describe the bug

I recently updated to Xcode 27.2, and now Briefcase can't start any simulator except an iPhone Duo.

### How to reproduce the bug

```
(bw-311) msmith@MacBook-Pro apps % briefcase new
[Accept default answers]
(bw-311) msmith@MacBook-Pro apps % cd helloworld 
(bw-311) msmith@MacBook-Pro helloworld % briefcase create ios
...
(bw-311) msmith@MacBook-Pro helloworld % briefcase build ios                                                               

[helloworld] Updating app metadata...
Setting main module... done

[helloworld] Building Xcode project...
Building... done

[helloworld] Built build/helloworld/ios/xcode/build/Debug-iphonesimulator/Hello World.app
(bw-311) msmith@MacBook-Pro helloworld % briefcase run ios                     

Unable to automatically select an iOS simulator; no "SE-class" iPhone simulator (e.g., an iPhone SE, or a similar "entry level" device) is available on iOS 27.2, and the choice is ambiguous.

Specify a device explicitly with -d/--device, or use -d with no value to select from the full list of available simulators.

Log saved to /Users/msmith/git/beeware/apps/helloworld/logs/briefcase.2026_11_14-18_43_18.run.log
```

[briefcase.2026_11_14-18_43_18.run.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34858629/briefcase.2026_11_14-18_43_18.run.log)

```
(bw-311) msmith@MacBook-Pro helloworld % briefcase run ios -d

In the future, you could specify this device by running:

    $ briefcase run iOS -d "iPhone Duo::iOS 27.2"

or:

    $ briefcase run iOS -d 51DD8293-72DF-4BC2-956D-9D261FF9AD07

[helloworld] Starting app on an iPhone Duo running iOS 27.2 (device UDID 51DD8293-72DF-4BC2-956D-9D261FF9AD07)

I was never given the option to select a different simulator.

+def check_committable_supported(n: NetworkType, component: Components) -> None:

---

EDIT by @FabianHofmann : 

The root cause for the following issue it the non-fail-fast assignment of a `committable` attribute to component which do not allow for it.  I updated the title of the issue. 

*Original issue below*

---

### Version Checks (indicate both or one)

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the lastest [release](https://github.com/pypsa/pypsa/releases) of PyPSA.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the current [`master`](https://github.com/pypsa/pypsa/tree/master) branch of PyPSA.


### Issue Description

When creating the model, the code crashes when there are storage-units present within the network only if set to True. From the create_model(), we are looping over the variable "Storage-units-p_dispatch" and "Storage-units-p_store". This results in adding the variable Storage-units_status twice causing the error. 

### Reproducible Example

```python
import logging
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pypsa

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s",
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def create_minimal_network(n_snapshots=24):
    """
    Create a minimal PyPSA network for testing rolling horizon dispatch.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    n_snapshots : int
        Number of hourly snapshots to create
        
    Returns
    -------
    pypsa.Network
        A minimal network with generator, load, and storage unit
    """
    # Create network
    n = pypsa.Network()
    
    # Create snapshots (hourly for one day)
    snapshots = pd.date_range("2024-01-01", periods=n_snapshots, freq="h")
    n.set_snapshots(snapshots)
    
    # Add buses
    n.add("Bus", "bus_0", v_nom=1.0)
    n.add("Bus", "bus_1", v_nom=1.0)
    
    # Add carrier
    n.add("Carrier", "gas", co2_emissions=0.2)
    n.add("Carrier", "battery", co2_emissions=0.0)
    
    # Add a gas generator - dispatchable
    n.add(
        "Generator",
        "gas_gen",
        bus="bus_0",
        carrier="gas",
        p_nom=100,  # MW
        marginal_cost=50,  # $/MWh
        committable=True,
        min_up_time=2,
        min_down_time=2,
        up_time_before=0,
        down_time_before=4,
    )
    
    n.add(
        "StorageUnit",
        "battery",
        bus="bus_0",
        carrier="battery",
        p_nom=50,  # MW charging/discharging capacity
        max_hours=4,  # 4-hour battery (50 MW * 4h = 200 MWh)
        efficiency_store=0.95,
        efficiency_dispatch=0.95,
        marginal_cost=1,  # Small cost to prefer generator over battery
        state_of_charge_initial=50,  # Start at 50 MWh
        committable=True,  # Set to False to avoid PyPSA bug with status variables
    )
    
    # Add load with varying demand (sinusoidal pattern)
    hours = range(n_snapshots)
    base_load = 60  # MW
    load_variation = 20  # MW
    load_profile = [
        base_load + load_variation * (0.5 + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * h / 24))
        for h in hours
    ]
    
    n.add("Load", "load", bus="bus_0", p_set=0)
    n.loads_t.p_set["load"] = load_profile
    
    # Add link between buses
    n.add(
        "Link",
        "link_0_1",
        bus0="bus_0",
        bus1="bus_1",
        p_nom=75,  # MW
        efficiency=0.98,
    )
    
    return n



def main():
    """Main execution function."""
    logger.info("Creating minimal network...")
    network = create_minimal_network(n_snapshots=24)
    
    logger.info("\nNetwork summary:")
    logger.info(f"Generators:\n{network.generators[['bus', 'carrier', 'p_nom', 'committable', 'marginal_cost']]}")
    logger.info(f"\nStorage Units:\n{network.storage_units[['bus', 'carrier', 'p_nom', 'max_hours', 'committable']]}")
    logger.info(f"\nLoads:\n{network.loads[['bus', 'p_set']]}")
    
    # Run rolling horizon optimization
    logger.info("\n" + "="*60)
    logger.info("Starting rolling horizon dispatch simulation")
    logger.info("="*60)
    
    network.optimize.optimize_with_rolling_horizon(
        snapshots=network.snapshots,
        horizon=6,  # 6-hour optimization periods
        overlap=0,  # No overlap in simplified version
        solver_name="highs",
        linearized_unit_commitment=False,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

title: The negation of an `Int` is `0 - x`: its overflow row, its guard and its range check
issue_title: examples/factorial.vera admits every `@Nat` in its contract but traps on overflow from 21

install_config.install: pip install -e ".[dev]" -q

gold_patch:
diff --git a/DE_BRUIJN.md b/DE_BRUIJN.md
index 2204bbb06..3f70ad949 100644
--- a/DE_BRUIJN.md
+++ b/DE_BRUIJN.md
@@ -221,7 +221,7 @@ The commutative-operations trap is more dangerous with same-type parameters. If
 
 ```vera
 private fn factorial(@Nat -> @Nat)
-  requires(true)
+  requires(@Nat.0 <= 20)
   ensures(@Nat.result >= 1)
   decreases(@Nat.0)
   effects(pure)
diff --git a/FAQ.md b/FAQ.md
index bdf03ede7..05f7ded70 100644
--- a/FAQ.md
+++ b/FAQ.md
@@ -105,7 +105,7 @@ The guarantee is exactly as wide as the query path, and no wider. Every string t
 
 ## Does the compiler prove division-by-zero, out-of-bounds indexing, etc. can't happen?
 
-Where the solver can decide the operation, yes; where it cannot, a runtime guard catches it. The verifier auto-synthesises a proof obligation at every primitive operation whose well-definedness depends on operand values, and discharges it from the surrounding preconditions and path conditions.  **Integer** division and modulo by zero have a `b != 0` obligation (E526); float division is exempt, since `f64.div` by zero yields inf or NaN rather than trapping; array indexing has a `0 <= i < array_length(arr)` obligation (E527); `@Nat` subtraction underflow and `@Int` → `@Nat` narrowing have `>=` / `>= 0` obligations (E502 / E503).  Unary negation of an `@Int` is the exception ([#1875](https://github.com/aallan/vera/issues/1875)), with no obligation and no guard, so `-@Int.0` with `@Int.0` at `INT_MIN` returns `INT_MIN`, where `0 - @Int.0` traps.  A function that declares `requires(@Int.1 != 0)` and performs `@Int.0 / @Int.1` is statically proven free of a zero divisor (its overflow obligation for `INT_MIN / -1`, E528, stays Tier 3, guarded by the run-time overflow trap); a function that declares `requires(true)` and performs `@Int.1 / @Int.0` is refused by `vera verify` (E526), not left to a runtime trap.  You discharge an obligation by encoding the constraint in a precondition (`requires(...)`), a guarding `if` (whose path condition holds in the relevant branch), or a refinement type (`{ @Int | @Int.0 != 0 }`); the verifier then proves it at every call site. +++ b/tests/test_negation_overflow_1875.py
@@ -0,0 +1,478 @@
+"""A unary negation of an `Int` is `0 - x`: one `int_overflow` row, one guard (#1875).
+
+`-@Int.0` at `INT_MIN` is `2^63`, which no `Int` holds.  The negation lowered
+to an unchecked `i64.sub` from zero, the obligation table listed no row for it
+and the verifier translated it over unbounded integers, so a bare negation
+returned `INT_MIN` there and every contract proved over a negation was false at
+that one input with `vera verify` clean.
+
+The rule is the subtraction's: a negation of an `Int` operand has the
+`int_overflow` row `0 - x` has, the same guarded lowering and the same range
+two-check.  A negated literal is that literal's value (spec §4.2), the
+negation of a `Nat` cannot leave the range, and a `Float64` negation is
+`f64.neg`; none of the three has a row.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import functools
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests import pipeline
+from vera.runtime.traps import WasmTrapError
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.matrix(decides=[
+    "vera/obligations/table.py", "vera/verifier.py", "vera/wasm/operators.py"])
+
+INT_MIN = -(2**63)
+INT_MAX = 2**63 - 1
+_EXAMPLES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "examples"
+
+# The program the issue reports, every member of its checklist but the example.
+_REPORTED = """\
+type NegPositive = { @Int | -@Int.0 > 0 };
+
+public fn plain_neg(@Int -> @Int)
+  requires(true)
+  ensures(true)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  -@Int.0
+}
+
+public fn magnitude(@Int -> @Int)
+  requires(true)
+  ensures(@Int.result >= 0)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  if @Int.0 < 0 then {
+    -@Int.0
+  } else {
+    @Int.0
+  }
+}
+
+public fn into_refined(@Int -> @NegPositive)
+  requires(@Int.0 < 0)
+  ensures(true)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  @Int.0
+}
+
+private fn wants_negative(@Int -> @Int)
+  requires(-@Int.0 > 0)
+  ensures(true)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  7
+}
+
+public fn calls_it(@Int -> @Int)
+  requires(@Int.0 < 0)
+  ensures(true)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  wants_negative(@Int.0)
+}
+"""
+
+
+def _overflow_rows(source: str) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
+    """Each `int_overflow` obligation `vera verify` records: its status and line."""
+    verified = pipeline.verify(source)
+    assert verified.ok, verified.diagnostics
+    return [(o.status, o.line) for o in verified.obligations
+            if o.kind == "int_overflow"]
+
+
+def _trap_kind(source: str, fn: str, arg: int) -> str | None:
+    """The trap kind ``fn(arg)`` ends with, or ``None`` when it returns."""
+    ran = pipeline.run(source, fn, [arg], capture_stderr=False)
+    try:
+        _ = ran.execution
+    except WasmTrapError as trap:
+        return trap.kind
+    return None
+
+
+def test_repro_1875_reported_program_records_a_row_per_negation() -> None:
+    """Every negation of an `Int` operand in the reported program carries the
+    row: the refinement predicate (line 1), `plain_neg`'s body (line 8),
+    `magnitude`'s branch (line 17) and `wants_negative`'s `requires`
+    (line 32).  None is proved: each admits `INT_MIN`, and each is the
+    run-time check that stops it there."""
+    rows = _overflow_rows(_REPORTED)
+    assert sorted(rows) == [("tier3", 1), ("tier3", 8), ("tier3", 17),
+                            ("tier3", 32)], rows
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fn", ["plain_neg", "magnitude", "into_refined", "calls_it"])
+def test_repro_1875_each_function_traps_with_overflow_at_int_min(fn: str) -> None:
+    """At `INT_MIN` each function stops at the negation with the overflow
+    trap, not with a wrong value or a contract proved at Tier 1."""
+    assert _trap_kind(_REPORTED, fn, INT_MIN) == "overflow"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fn", ["plain_neg", "magnitude", "into_refined", "calls_it"])

+    """One above `INT_MIN` no negation leaves the range: each function returns."""
+    assert _trap_kind(_REPORTED, fn, INT_MIN + 1) is None
+
+

+    assert verified.ok, verified.diagnostics
+    rows = [o.status for o in verified.obligations if o.kind == "int_overflow"]

+

+
+

+    """A predicate is verified once at its declaration (spec §6.4.3) under

+                  if o.kind == "int_overflow")
+    assert rows == [(1, "tier3"), (3, "verified")], verified.obligations
+
+
+#: A type no guard reads, one per operation a declaration takes by its own
+#: rule (`ContractVerifier._declaration_takes`), the line each stands on.
+_DECLARED = """\
+type IntSum = { @Int | @Int.0 + 1 > 0 };
+
+type NatSum = { @Nat | @Nat.0 + @Nat.0 >= 0 };
+
+type NatDiff = { @Nat | @Nat.0 - @Nat.0 == 0 };
+
+type NatNeg = { @Nat | -@Nat.0 <= 0 };
+
+type Magnitude = { @Int | abs(@Int.0) > 0 };
+
+type Truncated = { @Float64 | float_to_int(@Float64.0) > 0 };
+
+type Headed = { @Array<Int> | @Array<Int>.0[0] > 0 };
+
+type Asserted = { @Int | { assert(@Int.0 > 0); true } };
+
+type Called = { @Int | @Int.0 > 0 && positive(@Int.0) };
+
+type FloatSum = { @Float64 | @Float64.0 + 1.5 > 0.0 };
+
+type Pos = { @Int | @Int.0 > 0 };
+
+type Wrapped = { @Int | takes(mk(@Int.0)) };
+
+private fn positive(@Int -> @Bool)
+  requires(@Int.0 > 0)
+  ensures(true)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  true
+}
+
+private fn mk(@Int -> @Option<Int>)
+  requires(true)
+  ensures(true)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  Some(@Int.0)
+}
+
+private fn takes(@Option<Pos> -> @Bool)
+  requires(true)
+  ensures(true)
+  effects(pure)
+{
+  true
+}
+"""
+
+
+def test_repro_1875_each_declaration_takes_its_operations_rows() -> None:
+    """Verified at its declaration, each predicate holds exactly the rows
+    of the operations it performs: an `Int` sum's and a `Nat` sum's range,
+    a `Nat` difference's sign (no range), an `abs`, a float truncation, an
+    index, an `assert` and a call's precondition.  A `Nat` negation and a
+    `Float64` sum have none, and a call's argument is not the declaration's
+    narrowing to take."""
+    verified = pipeline.verify(_DECLARED)
+    assert verified.ok, verified.diagnostics
+    rows = sorted((o.line, o.kind, o.status) for o in verified.obligations
+                  if o.line < 24)
+    assert rows == [
+        (1, "int_overflow", "tier3"),
+        (3, "int_overflow", "tier3"),
+        (5, "nat_sub", "verified"),
+        (9, "int_overflow", "tier3"),
+        (11, "float_to_int_domain", "tier3"),
+        (13, "index_bounds", "tier3"),
+        (15, "assert", "tier3"),
+        (17, "call_pre", "verified"),
+    ], verified.obligations
+
+
+# =====================================================================
+# The class: a negation at every position, against its `0 - x` twin
+# =====================================================================
+#
+# The oracle is the subtraction the rule says a negation is.  Each cell
+# builds a program with the negation and its twin with `0 - x` in its place,
+# and holds the two to the same obligations (kind and status, all of them)
+# and the same run at the cell's value.  On top of the twin: the negation
+# traps with the overflow kind at `INT_MIN` wherever the compiled program
+# evaluates it, and nowhere else; where it traps, no `int_overflow` row
+# reads `verified`; and no cell's program is refused.
+
+_HEADER = "  requires(true)\n  ensures(true)\n  effects(pure)\n"
+_IDENT = ("\n\nprivate fn ident(@Int -> @Int)\n" + _HEADER
+          + "{\n  @Int.0\n}\n")
+
+
+def _body(expr: str, param: str = "@Int", ret: str = "@Int") -> str:
+    return f"public fn f({param} -> {ret})\n{_HEADER}{{\n  {expr}\n}}\n"
+
+
+def _position(pos: str, n: str) -> str:
+    """The program with the negated expression *n* at *pos*."""
+    if pos == "body":
+        return _body(n)
+    if pos == "requires":
+        return (f"public fn f(@Int -> @Int)\n  requires({n} != 5 || true)\n"
+                f"  ensures(true)\n  effects(pure)\n{{\n  @Int.0\n}}\n")
+    if pos == "ensures":
+        return (f"public fn f(@Int -> @Int)\n  requires(@Int.0 != -5)\n"
+                f"  ensures({n} != 5 || true)\n  effects(pure)\n{{\n  @Int.0\n}}\n")
+    if pos == "refinement":
+        return (f"type T = {{ @Int | {n} != 5 || true }};\n\n"
+                f"public fn f(@Int -> @Int)\n  requires(@Int.0 != -5)\n"
+                f"  ensures(true)\n  effects(pure)\n{{\n  let @T = @Int.0;\n"
+                f"  @Int.0\n}}\n")
+    if pos == "decreases":

+                f"  ensures(true)\n  decreases({n})\n  effects(pure)\n{{\n"

+    if pos == "assert":
+        return _body(f"assert({n} != 5 || true);\n  @Int.0")
+    if pos == "assume":
+        return _body(f"assume({n} != 5 || true);\n  @Int.0")
+    if pos == "closure":
+        return ("type IntToInt = fn(Int -> Int) effects(pure);\n\n"
+                + _body("let @IntToInt = fn(@Int -> @Int) effects(pure) "
+                        f"{{ {n} }};\n  apply_fn(@IntToInt.0, @Int.0)"))
+    if pos == "where":
+        return (_body("g(@Int.0)") + "where {\n  fn g(@Int -> @Int)\n"
+                "    requires(true)\n    ensures(true)\n    effects(pure)\n"
+                f"  {{\n    {n}\n  }}\n}}\n")
+    raise AssertionError(pos)
+
+
+def _unary(e: str) -> str:
+    return f"-({e})" if e.startswith("-") else f"-{e}"
+
+
+def _twin(e: str) -> str:
+    return f"(0 - {e})"
+
+
+#: The operand forms, each as the negated expression a negator builds.
+_FORMS: dict[str, Callable[[Callable[[str], str]], str]] = {
+    "slot": lambda neg: neg("@Int.0"),
+    "call": lambda neg: neg("ident(@Int.0)"),
+    "nested": lambda neg: neg(neg("@Int.0")),
+    "arith": lambda neg: neg("(@Int.0 * 1)"),
+}
+#: Where the compiled program evaluates nothing, nothing is obligated.
+_UNEVALUATED = {"assume"}
+_POSITIONS = ["body", "requires", "ensures", "refinement", "decreases",
+              "assert", "assume", "closure", "where"]
+_VALUES = {"int_min": INT_MIN, "int_min_plus_1": INT_MIN + 1, "minus_1": -1,
+           "zero": 0, "int_max": INT_MAX}
+
+
+def _program(pos: str, form: str, neg: Callable[[str], str]) -> str:
+    return _position(pos, _FORMS[form](neg)) + _IDENT
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _verified(source: str) -> tuple[bool, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...], str]:
+    v = pipeline.verify(source)
+    obligations = tuple(sorted((o.kind, o.status) for o in v.obligations)) if v.ok else ()
+    return v.ok, obligations, repr(v.diagnostics)
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _compiled(source: str) -> pipeline.Compiled:
+    return pipeline.compile(source)
+
+
+def _outcome(source: str, arg: int) -> tuple[str, object]:
+    ran = pipeline.run(_compiled(source), "f", [arg], capture_stderr=False)
+    try:
+        return ("value", ran.execution.value)
+    except WasmTrapError as trap:
+        return ("trap", trap.kind)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", list(_VALUES))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("form", list(_FORMS))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pos", _POSITIONS)
+def test_negation_is_its_subtraction(pos: str, form: str, value: str) -> None:
+    neg, twin = _program(pos, form, _unary), _program(pos, form, _twin)
+    n_ok, n_obligations, n_diags = _verified(neg)
+    t_ok, t_obligations, t_diags = _verified(twin)
+    assert n_ok, n_diags
+    assert t_ok, t_diags
+    assert n_obligations == t_obligations
+    arg = _VALUES[value]
+    got = _outcome(neg, arg)
+    assert got == _outcome(twin, arg)
+    traps = got == ("trap", "overflow")
+    assert traps == (arg == INT_MIN and pos not in _UNEVALUATED), got
+    if traps:
+        statuses = [s for k, s in n_obligations if k == "int_overflow"]
+        assert statuses and set(statuses) != {"verified"}, n_obligations
+
+
+# =====================================================================
+# The operand's type, and the literal
+# =====================================================================
+
+
+_TYPED = {
+    # name: (program, the int_overflow statuses, [(argument, outcome)])
+    "nat": (_body("-@Nat.0", "@Nat"), [],
+            [(0, ("value", 0)), (INT_MAX, ("value", -INT_MAX))]),
+    "float64": (_body("-@Float64.0", "@Float64", "@Float64"), [],
+                [(1.5, ("value", -1.5))]),
+    "refined_nat": ("type Small = { @Nat | @Nat.0 < 10 };\n\n"
+                    + _body("-@Small.0", "@Small"), [],
+                    [(9, ("value", -9))]),
+    "refined_bounded_int": ("type Small = { @Int | @Int.0 > -1000 && @Int.0 < 1000 };\n\n"
+                            + _body("-@Small.0", "@Small"), ["verified"],
+                            [(-999, ("value", 999))]),
+    "refined_negative_int": ("type Neg = { @Int | @Int.0 < 0 };\n\n"
+                             + _body("-@Neg.0", "@Neg"), ["tier3"],
+                             [(INT_MIN, ("trap", "overflow")),
+                              (INT_MIN + 1, ("value", INT_MAX))]),
+    "int_under_precondition": (
+        "public fn f(@Int -> @Int)\n  requires(@Int.0 > -9223372036854775808)\n"
+        "  ensures(@Int.result >= 0)\n  effects(pure)\n"
+        "{\n  if @Int.0 < 0 then {\n    -@Int.0\n  } else {\n    0\n  }\n}\n",
+        ["verified"], [(INT_MIN + 1, ("value", INT_MAX))]),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", list(_TYPED))
+def test_negation_by_operand_type(name: str) -> None:
+    """A `Nat` operand, a `Float64` and a refinement of `Nat` have no row; a
+    refinement of `Int` has the row, proved where its predicate excludes
+    `INT_MIN` and guarded where it does not."""
+    source, statuses, runs = _TYPED[name]
+    ok, obligations, diags = _verified(source)
+    assert ok, diags
+    assert [s for k, s in obligations if k == "int_overflow"] == statuses
+    for arg, outcome in runs:
+        assert _outcome(source, arg) == outcome  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+
+
+_MAGNITUDES = {"two_pow_63": 2**63, "int_max": INT_MAX, "one": 1, "zero": 0}
+_LITERAL_POSITIONS = ["body", "requires", "assert", "closure", "where"]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("magnitude", list(_MAGNITUDES))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("pos", _LITERAL_POSITIONS)
+def test_negated_literal_is_its_value(pos: str, magnitude: str) -> None:
+    """`-m` for a literal `m` is the constant `-m` (spec §4.2), `INT_MIN`
+    included: no row, no guard, at every position."""
+    lit = _MAGNITUDES[magnitude]
+    source = _position(pos, f"-{lit}") + _IDENT
+    ok, obligations, diags = _verified(source)
+    assert ok, diags
+    assert [s for k, s in obligations if k == "int_overflow"] == []
+    expected = -lit if pos in ("body", "closure", "where") else 3
+    assert _outcome(source, 3) == ("value", expected)
+
+
+# =====================================================================
+# E528 as written, for each operation it reports
+# =====================================================================
+
+_E528_RATIONALE = (
+    "@Int / @Nat arithmetic carries a Tier-1 proof obligation that the result "
+    "stays within the i64 range.  The SMT solver proved the result is always "
+    "out of range; `+`/`-`/`*`, negation and `abs` trap at runtime on "
+    "overflow (#798).")
+_E528_SPEC_REF = 'Chapter 6, Section 6.4.3 "Primitive Operation Safety"'
+
+
+def _e528_fix(written: str) -> str:
+    return (f"Constrain the operands so `{written}` cannot overflow — add a "
+            "precondition bounding them, give an operand a refinement type "
+            "that bounds its range, or guard the operation with a path "
+            "condition the obligation can discharge.")
+
+
+def _refuted(params: str, requires: str, ret: str, body: str) -> str:
+    return (f"public fn f({params} -> {ret})\n  requires({requires})\n"
+            f"  ensures(true)\n  effects(pure)\n{{\n  {body}\n}}\n")
+
+
+#: Each operation `_report_overflow` names, refuted at line 6, column 3:
+#: (the program, the operation's word, the operation as written, the
+#: counterexample's lines).
+_E528_FORMS = {
+    "addition": (_refuted("@Int", "@Int.0 == 9223372036854775807", "@Int", "@Int.0 + 1"),
+                 "addition", "@Int.0 + 1", ["@Int.0 = 9223372036854775807"]),
+    "subtraction": (_refuted("@Int", "@Int.0 == -9223372036854775807", "@Int", "@Int.0 - 2"),
+                    "subtraction", "@Int.0 - 2", ["@Int.0 = -9223372036854775807"]),
+    "multiplication": (_refuted("@Int", "@Int.0 == 9223372036854775807", "@Int", "@Int.0 * 2"),
+                       "multiplication", "@Int.0 * 2", ["@Int.0 = 9223372036854775807"]),
+    "negation": (_refuted("@Int", "@Int.0 == -9223372036854775808", "@Int", "-@Int.0"),
+                 "negation", "-@Int.0", ["@Int.0 = -9223372036854775808"]),
+    "abs": (_refuted("@Int", "@Int.0 == -9223372036854775808", "@Nat", "abs(@Int.0)"),
+            "`abs`", "abs(@Int.0)", ["@Int.0 = -9223372036854775808"]),
+    "quotient": (_refuted("@Int, @Int", "@Int.1 == -9223372036854775808 && @Int.0 == -1",
+                          "@Int", "@Int.1 / @Int.0"),
+                 "operation", "@Int.1 / @Int.0",
+                 ["@Int.0 = -1", "@Int.1 = -9223372036854775808"]),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("form", list(_E528_FORMS))
+def test_repro_1875_e528_as_written(form: str) -> None:
+    """The refuted overflow's diagnostic, every field whole: the operation's
+    word, its counterexample, the rationale, the fix naming the operation
+    as written, the section, and where it stands."""
+    source, word, written, counterexample = _E528_FORMS[form]
+    verified = pipeline.verify(source)
+    found = [(d.description, d.rationale, d.fix, d.spec_ref, d.severity,
+              d.location.line, d.location.column)
+             for d in verified.diagnostics if d.error_code == "E528"]
+    description = (f"Integer {word} in 'f' provably overflows.\n"
+                   "  Counterexample:\n"
+                   + "\n".join(f"      {line}" for line in counterexample))
+    assert found == [(description, _E528_RATIONALE, _e528_fix(written),
+                      _E528_SPEC_REF, "error", 6, 3)]

problem_statement.title: examples/factorial.vera admits every `@Nat` in its contract but traps on overflow from 21
problem_statement.body:
`factorial` in `examples/factorial.vera` declares `requires(true)` and `ensures(@Nat.result >= 1)`, so its contract admits every `@Nat`. But 21! is above u64.MAX, so from 21 on the multiplication overflows and the run traps instead of returning:

```
$ vera run examples/factorial.vera --fn factorial -- 20
2432902008176640000
$ vera run examples/factorial.vera --fn factorial -- 21
Error: Integer overflow
```

`vera verify` reports the multiplication's `int_overflow` obligation `tier3` (line 11, column 5), so the overflow guard is the only evidence for that site, and it fires on inputs the contract admits. The `ensures` is `verified`, because an overflow traps rather than returning a wrong value. The example therefore reads as a function proved for every `@Nat` when it can compute only 0 to 20. `vera test --distrust` (#1634) shows it: 80 of 100 generated inputs trap.

## Fix direction

State the domain the function has: `requires(@Nat.0 <= 20)`. The overflow stays a runtime check, since the verifier cannot bound `factorial(@Nat.0 - 1)` from `ensures(@Nat.result >= 1)`, but no admitted input reaches it. The recursive call's precondition follows from the caller's. The two inputs this example is run on today are inside the domain: `vera run examples/factorial.vera --fn factorial -- 10` in `examples/README.md`, and `test_factorial`'s `factorial(5)`.

Done when `vera test --distrust examples/factorial.vera` passes.

problem_statement.title: Geometry is not kept in sync with its cell and problem
problem_statement.body:
## Bug Description

A cell's geometry tree isn't kept in sync with the cell and its problem. `read_input` links every node to the cell through `HalfSpace._cell`, by way of `update_pointers`, but the other routes don't:

| Route | Nodes linked |
|---|---|
| `read_input` | All |
| `cell.geometry = ...` | Root only |
| `HalfSpace.left = ...` or `.right = ...` | None of the new nodes |
| `montepy.Cell("...")` | None |
| `cell.clone()` | Linked to a deep copy of the original cell, not to the clone |

`HalfSpace.replace` and the `UnitHalfSpace.divider` setter use the link to keep `Cell.surfaces` and `Cell.complements` up to date. This causes:

1. After `cell.geometry = ...`, `replace` on a tree with more than one leaf doesn't update `cell.surfaces`. If the cell is then appended to a problem, the old surface reaches `problem.surfaces` and the new one doesn't. Writing that problem gives an input that references an undefined surface, and reading it back raises `BrokenObjectLinkError`.
2. `replace` on a clone can raise `KeyError`.
3. Reassigning `cell.geometry` leaves the old surfaces and complements on the cell.
4. Changing the geometry of a cell that is already in a problem doesn't add new surfaces to the problem, through `replace`, `cell.geometry = ...`, or `&=`.
5. Setting `left` or `right` doesn't update the cell at all.

Found while working on #1033, where `HalfSpace.mcnp_str` looks up the version of the problem through this link.

## To Reproduce

``` python
import montepy


def plane(number):
    return montepy.AxisPlane(f"{number} PZ {float(number)}")


# 1. the setter only links the root
s1, s2, s3 = plane(1), plane(2), plane(3)
cell = montepy.Cell(number=1)
cell.geometry = -s1 & +s2
cell.geometry.replace(s1, s3)
problem = montepy.MCNP_Problem("foo")
problem.cells.append(cell)
print(cell.geometry)                         # (-3*+2)
print([s.number for s in cell.surfaces])     # [1, 2], expected [2, 3]
print([s.number for s in problem.surfaces])  # [1, 2], expected [2, 3]

# 2. clones are linked to a copy of the original cell
s1, s3 = plane(1), plane(3)
cell = montepy.Cell(number=1)
cell.geometry = -s1
clone = cell.clone()
print(clone.geometry._cell is clone)  # False
clone.geometry.replace(list(clone.surfaces)[0], s3)  # KeyError

# 3. reassigning leaves the old surfaces behind
s1, s2 = plane(1), plane(2)
cell = montepy.Cell(number=1)
cell.geometry = -s1
cell.geometry = -s2
print([s.number for s in cell.surfaces])  # [1, 2], expected [2]

# 4. parsed cells are not linked
cell = montepy.Cell("1 0 -1 imp:n=1")
print(cell.geometry._cell)  # None
```

## Error Message

Only case 2 raises at the time of the change:

<details open>

``` python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "example.py", line 10, in <module>
    clone.geometry.replace(list(clone.surfaces)[0], s3)
  File "montepy/surfaces/half_space.py", line 315, in replace
    container.remove(old_divider)
  File "montepy/numbered_object_collection.py", line 406, in remove
    raise KeyError(f"This object is not in this collection")
KeyError: 'This object is not in this collection'
```

</details>

## MCNP input file snippet

No input file is needed.

## Version

 - `1.5.1.dev104+gafa420935`, also reproduced on `1.5.0`

## Additional context

The setter can't be used from `_parse_geometry`, because it raises `IllegalState` on dividers that are still numbers, so the link needs a step that doesn't resolve them.

One related case is not covered by the fix I'm opening: setting `UnitHalfSpace.divider` directly doesn't remove the old divider from the cell or add the new one to the problem. `remove_duplicate_surfaces` goes through that setter, including during `Cell.clone`, so changing it needs more care. `HalfSpace.replace` is the route that handles both.

problem_statement.title: compute_fpp returns a larger value than compute_fvar for white noise
problem_statement.body:
**Gammapy version**
main at 37288a67. The line in question has not changed since `compute_fpp` was added in #4726.

**Bug description**
`compute_fpp` divides the sum of squared differences of consecutive points by `N - 1`. Eq. 3 of Edelson et al. (2002), which the docstring cites, has `2 (N - 1)`. For white noise `E[(x_{i+1} - x_i)^2] = 2 sigma^2`, so F_pp comes out too large.

**Expected behavior**
The docstring says F_pp and F_var give the same value for white noise.

**To Reproduce**
```python
import numpy as np
from gammapy.stats import compute_fvar, compute_fpp

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
flux = 10 + rng.normal(0, 2, 200_000) + rng.normal(0, 1, 200_000)  # intrinsic sigma 2, errors 1
flux_err = np.full(flux.size, 1.0)

print(compute_fvar(flux, flux_err)[0], compute_fpp(flux, flux_err)[0])
```
Expected about 0.2 for both. Output: `0.2000516...  0.3004934...`

**Other information**
I found this while reading the code. The fix is one line plus updated tests, and I am happy to open a PR.

problem_statement.title: list-overrides: use the package-level `source:` for variants without one
problem_statement.body:
## Problem

`list-overrides --details` decides whether a variant is prebuilt from the variant's own `source:`, or else from its `pre_built` flag ([list_overrides.py#L77-L84](https://github.com/python-wheel-build/fromager/blob/ccd98cc73fc580a5b806b84990dae92565fe8ce4/src/fromager/commands/list_overrides.py#L77-L84)). It ignores a package-level `source:`.

With this settings file, the `cpu` variant shows `yes` although its effective provider downloads prebuilt wheels:

```yaml
source:
  provider: pypi-prebuilt
variants:
  cpu:
    env:
      FOO: "1"
```

## Fix

Use the variant's `source:` if it has one, otherwise the package's `source:`, and read `resolves_prebuilt_wheel` from that. Fall back to `pre_built` only when neither has a `source:`. Add a test for this case.

Display only. Non-blocking for #1414. Reported by CodeRabbit on #1414.

+            and severity_number < self._logger_config.minimum_severity
+        ):
+            return False
+        if self._logger_config.trace_based:
+            span_context = get_current_span(context).get_span_context()
+            if span_context.is_valid and not span_context.trace_flags.sampled:
+                return False
         return self._multi_log_record_processor.enabled(
             context=context,
             instrumentation_scope=self._instrumentation_scope,

problem_statement.title: Logs Enabled: implement Development-status conditions (minimum_severity, trace_based)
problem_statement.body:
## What

Implement the remaining, Development-status conditions of the Logs `Enabled` spec in the SDK: severity-based filtering (`minimum_severity`) and trace-based filtering (`trace_based`).

## Background

PR #5380 adds `Logger.enabled()` and implements the **stable** conditions of the spec's [`Enabled` section](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/blob/main/specification/logs/sdk.md#enabled):

- there are no registered `LogRecordProcessors`
- `LoggerConfig.enabled` is `false` (handled in `Logger.enabled()`)
- all registered `LogRecordProcessors` implement `Enabled` and each returns `false`

The spec lists two further conditions under which `Enabled` MUST return `false`, both currently marked **[Development]**:

- the provided severity is specified (not `0`) and is less than the configured `minimum_severity`
- `trace_based` is `true` and the current context is associated with an unsampled trace

These were intentionally deferred out of #5380 (see https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/pull/5380#discussion_r3715247579 and the issue discussion at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python/issues/5360#issuecomment-5183215458).

## Why deferred

- Both conditions are still **Development** status in the spec and subject to change.
- `_LoggerConfig` currently only has `is_enabled`; these conditions require adding `minimum_severity` and `trace_based` fields to the config model first. The tracer analog `_TracerConfig` also only has `is_enabled`, so the config model should grow consistently across signals (related: #5524).

## Proposed scope

- Add `minimum_severity` and `trace_based` fields to `_LoggerConfig`.
- Have `Logger.enabled()` return `false` when the provided severity is below `minimum_severity`, and when `trace_based` is set and the current context is an unsampled trace.
- Track the spec closely, since these conditions are Development status.

cc @aabmass @herin049
